items.title: Skryabin's equivalence for the type-A Whittaker pair
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]], inherited from assertion (2) of the good-grading cohomology supplier.

Let $(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak p,\mathfrak h,\mathfrak m,e,\chi)$, $W(\lambda)$,
$Q_\chi$ and $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ be as in
[[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]. Then the functor
$$Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-\colon W(\lambda)\text{-mod}\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$$
is an equivalence of categories, with inverse the Whittaker-vector functor
$\mathrm{Wh}$; in particular $\mathrm{Wh}$ is exact and
$\mathrm{Wh}(M)=0$ implies $M=0$ for $M\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$.

For every finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, the exact functor
$?\otimes X\colon\mathcal C(\lambda)\to\mathcal C(\lambda)$ transports to the
exact functor
$$M\circledast X=\mathrm{Wh}\bigl((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X\bigr)$$
on $W(\lambda)$-mod, and whenever $M$ is a $\mathfrak p$-module viewed as a
$W(\lambda)$-module by restriction, the natural map
$$\mu_{M,X}\colon M\circledast X\to M\otimes X,\qquad (\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)\otimes x\mapsto um\otimes x,$$
is an isomorphism of $W(\lambda)$-modules. The associativity isomorphisms
$(M\circledast X)\circledast Y\cong M\circledast(X\otimes Y)$ are compatible,
and for the one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module $\mathbb C_c$ the resulting
isomorphism $\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$
is independent of the order of the composed associativity isomorphisms.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The bimodule $Q_\chi$, a $W(\lambda)$-module $M$, a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-module $X$, and the maps $\mu_{M,X}$; assume AC as specified above.

1.1 **Unit, membership and counit.** The shifted $\mathfrak m$ action on $Q_\chi$ lowers the bounded-below Kazhdan filtration: $(x-\chi(x))u1_\chi=[x,u]1_\chi$, and for negative doubled degree $-2r$ the commutator lowers filtration by $2r>0$. This proves local nilpotence on $Q_\chi\otimes_W M$ too, so the adjunction lands in $\mathcal C(\lambda)$. By [F1], its unit $M\to\mathrm{Wh}(Q_\chi\otimes_W M)$ is an isomorphism. For $N\in\mathcal C(\lambda)$, the triangle identity makes $\mathrm{Wh}(c_N)$ an isomorphism. Left exactness gives $\mathrm{Wh}(\ker c_N)=0$, hence $\ker c_N=0$ by detection. Now the short exact sequence with this injective counit has $H^1$ of its domain zero by [F1]; its cohomology sequence gives $\mathrm{Wh}(\operatorname{coker}c_N)=0$. Detection makes that cokernel zero. Thus the unit and counit are isomorphisms, proving the equivalence without presuming exactness of $\mathrm{Wh}$. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

1.2 Exactness and detection. Exactness of $\mathrm{Wh}$ follows because it is inverse to the exact functor $Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}-$ (tensoring with the right-free module $Q_\chi$ proved in the local cohomology supplier [F1]), and the detection statement is the case $H^0=0$ of [F1]. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 The transported tensor functor. For $M\in W(\lambda)$-mod and finite-dimensional $X$, the functor $M\mapsto\mathrm{Wh}((Q_\chi\otimes_{W(\lambda)}M)\otimes X)$ is exact in $M$ because the composed functors are exact; it is the transport of $?\otimes X$ across the equivalence. [F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Invertibility of the displayed tensor map.** Let $M$ be a $\mathfrak p$-module and put $N=Q_\chi\otimes_W M$. PBW gives representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$, and $\psi_M(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)=um$ is balanced because right multiplication by $\eta(w)$ changes $u$ to $uw$. Hence $\mu_{M,X}=(\psi_M\otimes1)|_{\mathrm{Wh}}$ is a defined linear map. Use [F4]'s finite flag of $X$. Each quotient of $N\otimes X_j$ by $N\otimes X_{j-1}$ is a finite direct sum of $N$, with trivial $\mathfrak m$ action on its finite factor. By [F1] it has vanishing positive twisted cohomology and invariants $M\otimes(X_j/X_{j-1})$. Induction and the long exact sequence give the same vanishing on each $N\otimes X_j$, and give short exact sequences on their invariant spaces. The map $\mu$ preserves these filtrations. On each successive quotient, the invariants are represented by $1_\chi\otimes m\otimes\bar x$ and $\psi_M$ sends them to $m\otimes\bar x$. Thus its quotient maps are identities; induction through the finite short exact sequences makes $\mu$ bijective. This argument holds for arbitrary $M$ and needs no cofree realization or completion of $M$. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.2 Associativity. The associativity isomorphisms of the transported functor are obtained by inserting the canonical associativity isomorphisms of the tensor product of $\mathfrak g$-modules into the definition of $\circledast$ and applying the inverse equivalence; they are compatible by the naturality of the unit and counit of the adjunction and by the coherence of the tensor associativity in $\mathcal C(\lambda)$. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 **Balancing and $W$-linearity.** PBW gives unique representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$, $u\in U(\mathfrak p)$, in $Q_\chi$. Define $\psi_M(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes m)=um$. Since the right action of $w\in W\subset U(\mathfrak p)$ sends this representative to $\eta(uw)1_\chi$, the formula is right-$W$-balanced: $(uw)m=u(wm)$. Moreover $\psi_M(\eta(v)q\otimes m)=v\psi_M(q\otimes m)$ for $v\in U(\mathfrak p)$. The shift $\eta$ adds a Lie character on $\mathfrak p$, so on its primitive generators, and hence multiplicatively on $U(\mathfrak p)$, $(\eta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Delta(v)=\Delta\eta(v)$. The $W$ action on the source Whittaker subspace is therefore $\Delta\eta(w)$, while the target restricted $\mathfrak p$-module $M\otimes X$ has action $\Delta(w)$. Applying $\psi_M\otimes\mathrm{id}$ to the displayed coproduct identity proves $\mu_{M,X}(wz)=w\mu_{M,X}(z)$. Together with step 2.1 this proves the actual stated $W$-module isomorphism. No equality with cofree evaluation or citation-only character-equation argument is used. [F2, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Independence of the order. For $X=V^{\otimes d}$ the isomorphism $\mu_d$ is the composite of the single-step maps $\mu_{\bullet,V}$; two different parenthesizations differ by the associativity isomorphisms of step 2.2, and both are restrictions of the balanced evaluation maps of step 3.1, applied with the same iterated coproduct on $U(\mathfrak p)$; coassociativity and the displayed shift identity make these maps equal. Therefore the resulting isomorphism $\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to V_c^{\otimes d}$ is independent of the composed associativity isomorphisms. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

references.title: Wee Liang Gan and Victor Ginzburg, Quantization of Slodowy slices, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2002, no. 5, 243-255 (complete 10-page arXiv article)
references.locator: Section 6, Theorem 6.1 and its proof, and Section 6.2: Skryabin's equivalence, exactness of Wh, and the statement that Wh(E)=0 implies E=0; the tensor identification via the Taylor solution is in the same section.

references.title: Jonathan Brundan and Alexander Kleshchev, Representations of shifted Yangians and finite W-algebras, Mem. Amer. Math. Soc. 196 (2008), no. 918 (complete 109-page arXiv memoir)
references.locator: Chapter 8, Section 8.1, printed pp. 88-92: Q_chi as a free right W(lambda)-module, Skryabin's equivalence, the inverse functor Wh, and the natural maps (8.2)-(8.6) identifying the transported tensor functors; Section 8.1 also contains the explicit Taylor/path matrices for the tensor identification.

items.axiom_use: Inherited AC from GG assertion (2) for arbitrary-module cohomology/equivalence and its transported tensor functor; its polynomial transverse product and detection assertions (1)/(3) remain choice-free.

items.title: The loop filtration on the type-A finite W-algebra has associated graded U(g^e)
items.statement:
Equip $W(\lambda)$ with the loop (good) filtration
$$F_rW(\lambda)=W(\lambda)\cap\bigoplus_{s\le r}U(\mathfrak p)_s$$
induced by the pyramid grading $\mathfrak p=\bigoplus_{r\ge0}\mathfrak g_r$ of
[[def-a-type-a-nilpotent-pyramid-good-grading-and-whittaker-character]], and
likewise for the shifted Yangian of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
Then the associated graded algebra $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)$ is
canonically isomorphic to the enveloping algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, viewed as
a graded algebra via the restriction of the pyramid grading, and the
isomorphism sends the leading symbol of the generator $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to
$(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, where the $e_{i,j;r}$ are the centralizer basis of the
pyramid. In particular $W(\lambda)$ is a filtered deformation of
$U(\mathfrak g^e)$, the loop filtration is separated, and the ordered
monomials in the generators $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$, form a basis of
$W(\lambda)$.

This filtration is not the Kazhdan filtration: the Kazhdan filtration has
associated graded the commutative Slodowy-slice algebra $\mathbb C[S]$, while
here $\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)=U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative in
general.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The PBW basis and leading-symbol data of [F1]-[F2].

1.1 **Actual ambient leading term.** Give a matrix unit $e_{a,b}\in\mathfrak p$ its good degree $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)$. In the explicit signed path formula a term of canonical degree $r+1$ with $k$ matrix-unit factors has good degree at most $r+1-k$; a diagonal scalar replacement only lowers that degree. Therefore only single-factor terms contribute in good degree $r$. Those terms sum to $(-1)^r\sum e_{a,b}$ over $\operatorname{row}(a)=i$, $\operatorname{row}(b)=j$, $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)=r$, namely $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. Products introduced by Gauss factorization or its inverse have at least two factors and have smaller good degree. Thus the leading homogeneous component of $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ in the actual graded algebra $U(\mathfrak p)$ is exactly $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$. This proves the leading-symbol claim using the path degrees rather than a claim that Gauss inversion alone supplies its sign. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 **Independence in the ambient enveloping algebra.** The elements $e_{i,j;r}$ form a homogeneous basis of the actual Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak g^e\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Extend that finite basis to a homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak p$, with an order extending the prescribed order of the centralizer basis. Enveloping PBW implies that the ordered monomials in the $e_{i,j;r}$ are linearly independent in $U(\mathfrak p)$, and that the natural homomorphism $U(\mathfrak g^e)\to U(\mathfrak p)$ is injective. Their products and brackets are the actual ambient products and brackets, including all boundary terms of the centralizer strings. No projection of a current bracket with an arbitrary out-of-range convention is needed. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 **Strictness of the loop basis.** The finite $T$ monomials form a vector-space basis of $W(\lambda)$ by [F1]. For a monomial with total loop degree $d$, step 1.1 says that its degree-$d$ homogeneous component in $U(\mathfrak p)$ is, up to the product of its displayed signs, the corresponding PBW monomial in $U(\mathfrak g^e)$. In any nonzero finite linear combination of $T$ monomials, take the largest total loop degree $d$. The degree-$d$ homogeneous component is nonzero by step 1.2, even when degree-zero generators occur. Thus that combination belongs to $\bigoplus_{s\le d}U(\mathfrak p)_s$ and not to $\bigoplus_{s<d}U(\mathfrak p)_s$. Consequently the intersection filtration in the Statement is exactly the span of $T$ monomials of total loop degree at most $d$, and their degree-$d$ symbols form a basis of its associated graded. This verifies symbol independence directly, rather than inferring it from independence of filtered elements. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **The graded algebra isomorphism.** For any subalgebra of a nonnegatively graded algebra with its intersection filtration, taking highest homogeneous components embeds its associated graded into that graded algebra: if a representative's component of degree $d$ is zero it already lies in filtration $d-1$, and multiplication agrees with multiplication of homogeneous components. Apply this to $W(\lambda)\subseteq U(\mathfrak p)$. Step 2.1 identifies its image with the span of the ordered monomials in $\mathfrak g^e$, which is precisely the embedded algebra $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ from step 1.2. Hence $\operatorname{gr}^{\mathrm{loop}}W(\lambda)\cong U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the identification sends the symbol of $T_{i,j}^{(r+1)}$ to $(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$ as asserted. [F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra, construct]

4.1 **Filtration and the second graded algebra.** Each generator has finite nonnegative good degree, and each element is a finite sum of $T$ monomials, so the loop filtration is exhaustive and bounded below with $F_{-1}=0$. The actual homogeneous decomposition in $U(\mathfrak p)$ and step 2.1 give separatedness. The finite basis is already established in [F1], and step 3.1 establishes its filtered deformation property. Independently, the Kazhdan filtration uses positive weights $\operatorname{col}(b)-\operatorname{col}(a)+1$ on $\mathfrak p$ and has associated graded $\mathbb C[S]$ by [F4]; in the doubled convention its weights are twice these. That graded algebra is commutative, whereas $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ is noncommutative whenever $\mathfrak g^e$ is nonabelian. These are the two claimed filtrations and their respective graded algebras. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: The degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra
items.statement:
Let $H_d$ be the degenerate affine Hecke algebra of
[[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] and let
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\dots,a_l)$ be a multiset of complex numbers, $l\ge1$. The
**degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra** is $H_0(\mathbf a)=\mathbb C$ for $d=0$, and for $d\ge1$ is the quotient
$$H_d(\mathbf a):=H_d\Big/\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^l(x_1-a_j)\Bigr),$$
the two-sided ideal being the one generated by the displayed polynomial
([[def-left-right-and-two-sided-ideal]], [[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]],
[[thm-quotient-ring-laws]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the tensor-realization verification below; the quotient definition itself is choice-free.

The verification below records the structure of $H_d(\mathbf a)$ used on this
page. A $\mathbb C$-basis is given by the ordered monomials
$$x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w,\qquad 0\le r_1,\dots,r_d<l,\ w\in S_d,$$
so that $\dim H_d(\mathbf a)=l^dd!$; the polynomial-degree filtration has
associated graded the algebra
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1^l,\dots,x_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$. For
integral roots $a_j\in\mathbb Z$ this is the cyclotomic quotient $H_d(\Lambda)$
attached to the dominant weight $\Lambda=\sum_j m_j\Lambda_j$ of the integer
type-A root system, with $m_j=\#\{i:a_i=j\}$; for general complex roots one
uses a separate integer chain in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$, and the
symbol $\Lambda_a$ denotes a formal fundamental weight on that chain, not an
index of the integer-only lattice. The pyramid roots of the finite-W-algebra
constructions are $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for the origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ and the
pyramid columns $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. If $l=1$, then
$x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ in the quotient. The generator-fixing
anti-involution of $H_d$ descends to $H_d(\mathbf a)$. The top coefficient
functional of the monomial basis is a nondegenerate symmetric trace on
$H_d(\mathbf a)$, and it restricts to a nondegenerate trace on every central
block corner.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** $A=H_d/(f(x_1))$, the polynomial-degree filtration, and F1–F5; assume AC for F3 and the transported representation.

1.1 Bounded spanning in every variable. For each $r$, put $w_r=s_{r-1}\cdots s_1$ (and $w_1=1$). In the affine algebra the cross relations give $w_rx_1w_r^{-1}=x_r+$ terms of polynomial degree zero. Hence $w_rf(x_1)w_r^{-1}=x_r^l+$ terms of degree at most $l-1$. This element is zero in $A$. Every affine ordered monomial with an exponent at least $l$ can therefore have a factor $x_r^l$ replaced by terms of strictly smaller total polynomial degree; straightening those terms never increases that degree. Induction on total degree, applied to every such replacement, expresses every monomial as a linear combination of $x_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$ with $0\le r_i<l$. The same induction proves that $F_mA$ is spanned by bounded monomials of degree at most $m$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 A realization for arbitrary complex roots. For $d\ge1$ choose an integer $n\ge d$ and the rectangular partition $\lambda=(l,\ldots,l)$ with $n$ rows, so every column has height $q_j=n$ and $e$ has $n$ strings of length $l$. On $\mathfrak p$ define the one-dimensional module $\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}$ by $E_{ab}\mapsto\delta_{ab}a_{\mathrm{col}(a)}$. This is a Lie character: it vanishes on the strictly positive nilradical and is $a_j$ times the trace on the $j$th Levi block. In particular no integrality or coset condition on $a_j$ is needed. Restrict this module to $W$ and use F3 with $X=V^{\otimes d}$. Restrict the affine Hecke operators on $(Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_{\mathbf a})\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ to Whittaker vectors, then transport through F3. This defines an affine Hecke action on $V_{\mathbf a}^{\otimes d}=\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}\otimes V^{\otimes d}$; the $s_i$ are place permutations. The following step computes $x_1$ before asserting any quotient factorization. [F2, F3, F4, construct]

1.3 The transported first operator. Write $Q_c=Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_{\mathbf a}$ and define $\pi_c:Q_c\to\mathbb C$ by $\pi_c(\eta(u)1_\chi\otimes1)=u\cdot1$. It is well defined: the right $W$-relations become multiplication by the restricted character, and PBW gives representatives $\eta(u)1_\chi$. For a tensor basis vector $v_{\mathbf j}$ write its unique Whittaker preimage under F3 as $z=\sum_{\mathbf i}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes v_{\mathbf i}$, with $z_{\mathbf i}\in Q_c$. Then $\pi_c(z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$. If $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$, then $E_{ab}\in\mathfrak p$ and $\pi_c(E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i})=\delta_{ab}(a_{\mathrm{col}(a)}+\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h-n)\delta_{\mathbf i,\mathbf j}$, since $\eta^{-1}(E_{ab})=E_{ab}-\delta_{ab}(n-\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(a)}q_h)$. If $\mathrm{col}(a)>\mathrm{col}(b)$, the Whittaker equation for $E_{ab}$ instead gives $E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}=\chi(E_{ab})z_{\mathbf i}-\sum_{\mathbf k}z_{\mathbf k}$, where $\mathbf k$ runs over tensors obtained from $\mathbf i$ by replacing an occurrence of $a$ by $b$. Apply $\pi_c\otimes1$ to $\Omega_{01}z=\sum_{a,b,\mathbf i}E_{ab}z_{\mathbf i}\otimes E_{ba}^{(1)}v_{\mathbf i}$. The terms with $\mathrm{col}(a)\le\mathrm{col}(b)$ give $(a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}+\sum_{h\ge\mathrm{col}(j_1)}q_h-n)v_{\mathbf j}$. The $\chi$ term gives $v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}$, because $\chi(E_{ab})=1$ exactly when $b=L(a)$. In the negative sum, replacing the first occurrence gives $-\sum_{h>\mathrm{col}(j_1)}q_h\,v_{\mathbf j}$; replacing an occurrence in position $k>1$ gives $-v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}$ exactly when $\mathrm{col}(j_k)<\mathrm{col}(j_1)$. Consequently the transported right action is
$$v_{\mathbf j}x_1=v_{L_1(\mathbf j)}+(a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}-n)v_{\mathbf j}-\sum_{k>1:\ \mathrm{col}(j_k)<\mathrm{col}(j_1)}v_{\mathbf j\cdot(1\ k)}.$$
Here a nonexistent left-shift term is zero. In our rectangle $q_j=n$, so the diagonal coefficient is precisely $a_{\mathrm{col}(j_1)}$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 The cyclotomic relation and the leading symbols. Let $C_k$ be the span of tensors whose first entry has column at most $k$, with $C_0=0$. Step 1.3 gives $C_k(x_1-a_k)\subseteq C_{k-1}$: both the left shift and every exchange strictly lower the first column, while $x_1$ preserves $C_{k-1}$. Thus successively applying $(x_1-a_l),\ldots,(x_1-a_1)$ kills $C_l=V^{\otimes d}$. The factors commute, so $f(x_1)=0$ and the action factors through $A$. Grade $V$ by $\deg v_b=l-\mathrm{col}(b)$ and give its endomorphism algebra the induced filtration. In step 1.3 the left shift has degree one and every other term has total tensor degree zero. Hence $\operatorname{gr}_1x_1=e_1$. The recursion $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ shows by induction that all $x_j$ are filtered of degree one with leading symbol $e_j$, and that $s_j$ have degree zero with symbols the place permutations. [F1, F5, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Independence and the associated graded algebra. The cross relations and the conjugated relations in step 1.1 give a surjection $B=\mathbb C[X_1,\ldots,X_d]/(X_1^l,\ldots,X_d^l)\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}A$. Its composite with the associated graded tensor representation is $X_j\mapsto e_j$, $w\mapsto$ place permutation. Choose the rightmost box in each of $d$ distinct rows and let $v$ be the tensor of those boxes. For bounded $\mathbf r$ and $w$, the vectors $v e_1^{r_1}\cdots e_d^{r_d}w$ are distinct tensor basis vectors: their row labels identify the permutation, and their columns identify all $r_i$. Therefore this composite is injective. It follows that $B\cong\operatorname{gr}A$. Taking leading symbols of a hypothetical linear relation among bounded monomials, first in its largest total degree and then inductively, proves their independence. Along with step 1.1 this gives the claimed PBW basis, its filtration compatibility, and $\dim A=l^dd!$. The longest strings have length $l$, the number of columns, and there are $n=q_l\ge d$ of them; no column height is used as their length. For $d=0$ the algebra, basis and associated graded are all $\mathbb C$, so the assertions hold directly. [F1, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Integral roots and the pyramid dictionary. For integral roots write $m_i=\#\{j:a_j=i\}$; then $f(x_1)=\prod_i(x_1-i)^{m_i}$, the quotient attached to $\Lambda=\sum_i m_i\Lambda_i$. For arbitrary complex roots the same algebraic definition applies, with integer-chain bookkeeping separately in each coset of $\mathbb C/\mathbb Z$. The rectangle above has $c_j=a_j$ and $q_j=n$, hence $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$; the general pyramid dictionary is the displayed diagonal term of step 1.3. No general complex root is identified with an integer-only fundamental-weight index. [step 1.3, step 3.1, algebra]

4.2 Level one and the anti-involution. For $l=1$, $x_1=a_1$ and $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$ give $x_j=a_1+\sum_{k<j}(k\ j)$ by induction; the basis of step 3.1 identifies the quotient with $\mathbb C[S_d]$. The generator-fixing anti-involution fixes $f(x_1)$ and preserves its two-sided ideal, so descends to $A$. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

4.3 The graded top pairing. Put $D=d(l-1)$ and $T=x_1^{l-1}\cdots x_d^{l-1}$. Let $\tau_0:B\to\mathbb C$ be the coefficient of $X_1^{l-1}\cdots X_d^{l-1}\cdot1$. For graded monomials $X^{\mathbf r}w,X^{\mathbf s}v$, this coefficient is one exactly when $wv=1$ and $\mathbf r+w(\mathbf s)=(l-1,\ldots,l-1)$, and is zero otherwise. The equivalent reversed condition is $vw=1$ and $\mathbf s+w^{-1}(\mathbf r)=(l-1,\ldots,l-1)$; thus $\tau_0$ is symmetric. Each basis element pairs with its unique complementary element, so the pairing is perfect, including between degrees $m$ and $D-m$. Define $\tau:A\to\mathbb C$ as the coefficient of $T\cdot1$ in the PBW basis. By filtration compatibility $\tau=\tau_0\circ\operatorname{gr}_D$ on $A=F_DA$, and it vanishes on $F_{D-1}A$. Therefore, if $a\in F_mA$ and $b\in F_{D-m}A$, then $\tau(ab)=\tau_0(\operatorname{gr}_m(a)\operatorname{gr}_{D-m}(b))=\tau(ba)$. This establishes cyclicity only under the stated degree bound so far. [F5, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Full generator cyclicity. Since permutations have degree zero, step 4.3 gives $\tau(aw)=\tau(wa)$ for every $a\in A$, $w\in S_d$. To check $\tau(x_i b)=\tau(bx_i)$ for all bounded basis monomials $b$, step 4.3 suffices when $\deg b<D$. The remaining ones are exactly $b=Tw$. The polynomial $T$ is central: it commutes with the $x_j$, and the cross relations directly give $s_j(x_jx_{j+1})=(x_jx_{j+1})s_j$, while $s_j$ commutes with the other variables. Hence $s_jT=Ts_j$. Applying the already proved permutation cyclicity twice gives $\tau(x_iTw)=\tau(wx_iT)=\tau(wTx_i)=\tau(Twx_i)$. This proves cyclicity with every generator on every element; successively moving generators of a word from the beginning to the end proves $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ for all $a,b\in A$. It also covers $l=1$ (where $T=1$ and $D=0$). [F1, step 4.3, algebra]

6.1 Nondegeneracy and block restriction. For $0\ne a\in A$, take its largest filtration degree $m$, so $\operatorname{gr}_m(a)\ne0$. By the perfect graded pairing of step 4.3 choose homogeneous $b_0\in B_{D-m}$ with $\tau_0(\operatorname{gr}_m(a)b_0)\ne0$, and lift it to $b\in F_{D-m}A$. Then $\tau(ab)\ne0$. Thus the pairing has zero left radical, and symmetry gives zero right radical; this proves nondegeneracy without claiming that products of excess total degree have zero trace. If $e$ is a central idempotent and $0\ne a\in eA$, choose $b$ as above; then $\tau(aeb)=\tau(ab)\ne0$, so the restriction to $eA=eAe$ is nondegenerate and symmetric as well. [F5, step 4.3, step 5.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: The deformed tensor space for the type-A finite W-algebra
items.statement:
Fix the pyramid $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, its box-labelled natural module $V=\mathbb C^N$,
an arbitrary origin $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)\in\mathbb C^l$, and $d\ge0$.
Assume AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the imported Skryabin and Vust inputs.
For $X\in\mathfrak p$ define the column-trace character
$$\kappa_c(X)=\sum_{b=1}^l c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb}),$$
where $X_{bb}$ is its $b$th column-Levi diagonal block. Write
$\eta_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ for the resulting automorphism of $U(\mathfrak p)$,
so $\eta_c(e_{a,b})=e_{a,b}+\delta_{a,b}c_{\operatorname{col}(a)}$.
Let $\mathbb C_c$ be the corresponding one-dimensional $\mathfrak p$-module
and set $a_b=c_b+q_b-n$ and $\Lambda=\sum_{b=1}^l\Lambda_{a_b}$, with a
separate integer chain for each complex coset as in
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].

The **truncated (deformed) tensor space** $E_c=V_c^{\otimes d}$ is
$E=V^{\otimes d}$ with the left $U(\mathfrak p)$-action obtained by composing
the ordinary total tensor representation $\rho_d$ with $\eta_c$.
Equivalently it is $\mathbb C_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, with one character
factor; the origin twist is applied once to the total action. For $d\ge1$
its right $H_d(\Lambda)$-action is determined by place permutations $s_i$ and
$$x_1\mapsto\Bigl(e+\sum_{j=1}^N(c_{\operatorname{col}(j)}+q_{\operatorname{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}\Bigr)\otimes1^{\otimes(d-1)}-\sum_{k=2}^d\sum_{\operatorname{col}(i)<\operatorname{col}(j)}e_{i,j}\otimes1^{\otimes(k-2)}\otimes e_{j,i}\otimes1^{\otimes(d-k)},$$
with $x_{j+1}=s_jx_js_j+s_j$. Here the generator-fixing anti-involution of
the Hecke algebra converts the displayed operators into a right action.
For $d=0$ there are no $x_j,s_i$, $H_0(\Lambda)=\mathbb C$, and $E_c=\mathbb C_c$.

Grade the box basis by $\deg v_a=l-\operatorname{col}(a)$, use the total
tensor grading and its induced endomorphism filtration, and use the fixed
loop chart $\zeta\colon\operatorname{gr}W(\lambda)\to U(\mathfrak g^e)$ of
[[thm-the-loop-filtration-on-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-has-associated-graded-u-of-g-e]]:
$\zeta(\operatorname{gr}_rT_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^re_{i,j;r}$, $(i,j,r)\in K$.
The coefficient index remains the actual unshifted $T=FDE$ index of
[[def-shifted-yangian-and-pyramid-generators-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]].
The restricted character on the fixed centralizer basis is
$$\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c),\qquad \sigma_i(c)=\sum_{b=1}^{p_i}c_b.$$
Consequently the **full graded left representation** in this fixed chart is
$$\varphi_{d,c}(X)=\sum_{t=1}^d X^{(t)}+\kappa_c(X)\operatorname{id}_E\qquad(X\in\mathfrak g^e),$$
where $X^{(t)}$ acts in tensor position $t$. In particular its complete
mode-symbol dictionary is
$$\operatorname{gr}_r\Phi_{d,c}(T_{i,j}^{(r+1)})=(-1)^r\left(\sum_{t=1}^d e_{i,j;r}^{(t)}+\delta_{i,j}\delta_{r,0}\sigma_i(c)\operatorname{id}_E\right),$$
where $\Phi_{d,c}$ is the restricted $W(\lambda)$-action. On the right,
$\operatorname{gr}_1x_j=e^{(j)}$ and $\operatorname{gr}_0s_i$ is the place
permutation. Thus the graded bimodule is the character-twisted Vust module
$\mathbb C_{\kappa_c|\mathfrak g^e}\otimes E$, with the ordinary truncated
polynomial/permutation action. It need not be the untwisted Vust module in
the fixed chart. Nevertheless its unital left image algebra and its
commutant are exactly the untwisted Vust image algebra and commutant, as
proved below.

The displayed right operators commute with $W(\lambda)$; full
$\mathfrak p$-commutation is not asserted. They make $E_c$ a filtered
$(W(\lambda),H_d(\Lambda))$-bimodule. The actual balanced Skryabin map gives
a coherent isomorphism
$\mu_d\colon\mathbb C_c\circledast V^{\circledast d}\to E_c$ of
$(W(\lambda),H_d)$-bimodules. For every complex origin, every pyramid and
every $d$, the two filtered image algebras are mutual centralizers, and their
associated graded image algebras are the unital Vust image algebras. No
admissibility or stable-range restriction enters this centralizer assertion.

If the pyramid is empty, $N=l=0$, use $V=0$ and $W=U(\mathfrak g^e)=\mathbb C$.
For $d=0$ all structures are scalar; for $d>0$, $E=0$ and the empty
cyclotomic product is $1$, giving the zero quotient and zero endomorphism
algebra. All formulas and centralizer identities then have these evident
empty interpretations.
items.strategy: Assume AC for the actual Skryabin and Vust suppliers. The column-trace Lie character $\kappa_c(X)=\sum_b c_b\operatorname{tr}(X_{bb})$ defines the total origin twist once. Use the actual balanced $\mu$ and ambient trace-form Casimir; evaluation on its Whittaker preimages separates nonnegative-column terms, negative character terms, first-position replacements and cross-position replacements, giving exactly the displayed raw $x_1$. Thus affine relations and commutation are transported with $W$, not with all of $\mathfrak p$. First-column filtration gives the full cyclotomic polynomial, and the total tensor grading gives its exact minimal degree, including repeated roots. Restrict the column character to the fixed basis: $\kappa_c(e_{i,j;r})=\delta_{ij}\delta_{r0}\sum_{b\le p_i}c_b$. The graded automorphism $\tau_c(X)=X+\kappa_c(X)1$ preserves $U(\mathfrak g^e)$, and the full fixed-chart graded representation is $\operatorname{gr}\Phi_{d,c}=\varphi_{d,0}\tau_c\zeta$, including its surviving degree-zero scalar. Keep the actual $T=FDE$ coefficient index, $T^{(r+1)}$ loop degree $r$ and sign $(-1)^r$. The right symbols are individual $e$ operators and places. Since $\tau_c$ is a unital automorphism, the exact character-twisted representation has the same unital graded image and commutant as untwisted Vust. Prove the two full filtered centralizer identities by the chains $A^0\subseteq\operatorname{gr}C\subseteq\operatorname{gr}Z(D)\subseteq Z(\operatorname{gr}D)\subseteq Z(D^0)=A^0$ and its reverse counterpart, then finite descending subtraction. Handle $d=0$ with the nontrivial character on the scalar module and the empty pyramid by its zero/scalar identities. Rank-one $c_1=1,d=1$ yields fixed generator $E_{11}=2$, not untwisted $1$; the $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ example gives $[E_{11}-E_{22},x_1]=2E_{12}\ne0$. All origins, shapes and degrees are retained; no stable range or admissibility is used. Mathematical acceptance and actual-supplier/consumer closure remain with the original reviewer.

items.title: The parabolic highest-weight truncation factors through the cyclotomic quotient
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]] only for the imported
Skryabin equivalence identifying the raw Whittaker bimodule and its affine
action. The finite raw-matrix polynomial and minimal-polynomial calculations
and the ordinary $P_c\otimes V$ column-flag calculation are choice-free.

Let $\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a nonempty pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l>0$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be arbitrary complex origins,
and put $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$ for $1\le j\le l$. For $d\ge1$ consider the raw
tensor operator $x_1$ on the truncated tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ of
[[def-deformed-tensor-space-for-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra]] (whose underlying
space is $V^{\otimes d}$ and whose $x_1$ is the operator displayed there).
Then the minimal polynomial of $x_1$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is exactly
$$\prod_{j=1}^l(x-a_j),$$
including repeated roots with their multiplicities. Consequently the action of
$H_d$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ factors through the cyclotomic quotient
$H_d(\mathbf a)$ of [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]. The same
polynomial annihilates the action of the ordinary Casimir operator on
$P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, where $P_c$ is the ground induced module with its
genuine column filtration.

The statement does not assert that every unrelated standard object $N(A)$, or
every parabolic category-$\mathcal O$ object, carries that same tensor action.
For $d=0$ there is no operator $x_1$. The integral-root weight $\Lambda$ and
the arbitrary-root coset bookkeeping are the separate conventions of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]].
items.strategy: Define the full raw operator locally with the sum over every later tensor position $k=2,\ldots,d$, using the same physical box labels and arbitrary origins. Assume AC only for the actual Skryabin equivalence used to establish this raw affine action: evaluate its balanced tensor map on actual Whittaker preimages and separate the diagonal, negative character, first-position and later-position terms to recover the raw display. This model is $Q_\chi\otimes_W\mathbb C_c$, not the ordinary ground module. The first-column flag $C_b$ satisfies $C_b(x_1-a_b)\subseteq C_{b-1}$, so every column factor, including repeated roots, annihilates in succession. With total grading $\deg v_j=l-\operatorname{col}(j)$, the left shift has degree one and each cross-position exchange degree zero; hence $\operatorname{gr}_1x_1=e^{(1)}$, and nonvanishing powers below $l$ prove exact minimal degree. The affine action therefore factors through the cyclotomic quotient. Separately define the ordinary ground module $P_c=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak p)}\mathbb C_\mu$, with $\mu_b=c_b+\sum_{h\le b}q_h-n$. PBW right-freeness and the coproduct tensor identity induce the natural column flag on $P_c\otimes V$, not on $P_c$ itself. On a ground tensor $m_0\otimes v_j$, $\Omega=\sum E_{ab}\otimes E_{ba}$ contributes $\mu_b$ from the diagonal, zero from non-diagonal parabolic terms, and subtracts one for each earlier-column box after rewriting the lower-block term through the tensor identity. The other term lands in the earlier flag piece. Thus the quotient scalar is $\mu_b-\sum_{h<b}q_h=c_b+q_b-n=a_b$. Ambient $\mathfrak g$-linearity extends this to the entire quotient and preserves the flag, proving the same annihilating polynomial on $P_c\otimes V$. Tensoring the remaining factors proves the ordinary $P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ claim. Handle $d=0$ without a nonexistent $x_1$. Preserve arbitrary complex origins, every nonempty shape and repeated-root multiplicities. The Deformed definition is declared for the retained actual model context after its redundant dependence on this lemma is removed; the proof calculations remain local. No ordinary-to-plain-Skryabin identification, FDE reindexing or integral-category identification is used.

items.title: Separated integral cosets give typed parabolic category equivalences
items.statement:
Assume AC. Work in genuine type-$A$ parabolic category $\mathcal O$ for
$\mathfrak{gl}_N(\mathbb C)$ with its fixed Borel. Its column Levi has ordered
blocks of heights $q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$. All entries in column $j$ lie in
$c_j+\mathbb Z$, where the original admissibility condition is
$c_j-c_k\in\mathbb Z\Rightarrow c_j=c_k$. Use the source highest-weight
convention $\eta_i=a_i+i-1$ and half-sum
$\rho_i=(N+1-2i)/2$, with the column reading prescribed by the source Borel.
For each occurring entry coset $\kappa$ retain its columns in their original
order. Fix an order on the finite set of cosets; no order on $\mathbb C$ is used.

Subject to the local HC tensor-projective comparison stated in [F1], stable
sorting of the coordinates by $\kappa$ gives an exact, complex-linear
equivalence of the genuine parabolic categories, carrying each ordinary
Verma label by the dot permutation and carrying the corresponding generalized
standard, simple head and projective cover. On each linkage block, the sorted
category is equivalent to the product of the corresponding parabolic blocks
for $\mathfrak{gl}_{N_\kappa}$, where
$N_\kappa=\sum_{j\in\kappa}q_j$. Product means the abelian category generated
by finite presentations of outer tensor products, equivalently modules over
the tensor product of the finite block endomorphism algebras.

For the original pyramid with $n$ rows put $n_\kappa=\max_{j\in\kappa}q_j$.
The component integral entry dictionary is exactly
$$a_i^{\mathrm{int}}=a_i-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa,\qquad m_j=q_j-n_\kappa,\qquad \inf I_\kappa=1-n_\kappa.$$
Thus $m_j+1-\inf I_\kappa=q_j$, with the original nonincreasing retained
heights and charges. For the admitted-ground subcategories, where each original entry has a
nonnegative integral difference from its own ground entry, this dictionary
lands in the bounded-below admitted integral component models of [F4]. For
other genuine parabolic blocks it records the integral weight/coset
dictionary and the trace shift, without asserting membership in that fixed
admitted cut. If the component follows $B_\kappa$ sorted coordinates, its
Levi highest weight and the integral highest weight differ by the scalar
trace-character shift
$$\delta_\kappa=B_\kappa+c_\kappa-n+n_\kappa.$$
This shift is a Lie algebra character and requires no integrality of
$c_\kappa$. Singular repeated-entry linkage blocks are included. The original
complex origins, component entry multisets and their scalar centres remain
recorded; different complex cosets are not merged into one integral block.

Sorting commutes coherently with finite tensoring and its invariant Casimir
and permutation maps. The separated product decomposition is blockwise and
does not assert that unrestricted tensoring is componentwise. The proof gives
its actual filtration and block-projection comparison. Choices of sorting
word with the same stable permutation yield the natural comparison fixed on
the chosen reference highest vector and its tensor-projective presentations.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** Use the data of the Statement and [F1]–[F5]. Normalize Chevalley matrices by $E=E_{i,i+1}$, $F=E_{i+1,i}$ and $H=[E,F]$. Twist by $\phi=\exp(\operatorname{ad}E)\exp(\operatorname{ad}(-F))\exp(\operatorname{ad}E)$ with twisted action $x\cdot v=\phi(x)v$.

1.1 Every $H$-weight in the relevant weight-coset category is nonintegral when the adjacent shifted coordinates belong to different entry cosets: $\eta(H)=(\eta+\rho)_i-(\eta+\rho)_{i+1}-1$, and weight changes are integral. This holds in every subquotient. If $Fv=0$ for a weight vector of weight $h$, choose $r\ge0$ maximal with $E^rv\ne0$, using positive-root local nilpotence in $\mathcal O$. The $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation gives $FE^{r+1}v=-(r+1)(h+r)E^rv$, a contradiction. Thus $F$ is injective on every object and subquotient of that category. [given, algebra]

2.1 Powers of $F$ satisfy both Ore conditions in $U(\mathfrak g)$: iterating $Fu=uF+[F,u]$ gives the finite binomial commutation formula, since $\operatorname{ad}F$ is locally nilpotent on each enveloping element. PBW makes $U$ a domain. Its localization $U_F=\bigcup_{k\ge0}F^{-k}U$ is a directed union of free right $U$-modules; consequently localization $M_F=U_F\otimes_U M$ is exact. Step 1.1 makes $M\to M_F$ injective, and the diagram of short exact sequences $0\to M\to M_F\to M_F/M\to0$ proves exactness of $C_F(M)=M_F/M$. Therefore $T_s(M)={}^{\phi}C_F(M)$ is exact. The adjoint exponentials defining $\phi$ are finite on every $u\in U$; they send $E,F,H$ to $-F,-E,-H$ and act as the adjacent permutation on the Cartan. [F2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Let $v$ be the normalized highest vector of $\Delta_\eta$. The class $F^{-1}v$ becomes a highest vector of weight $s\cdot\eta$: its new $E$ is $-F$, whose value lies in $\Delta_\eta$; the other transformed positive roots are positive roots distinct from $\alpha_i$, and commuting them through $F^{-1}$ leaves positive-root terms killing $v$. The new $F$ sends $F^{-r}v$ to $r(\eta(H)+r+1)F^{-r-1}v$, with every scalar nonzero. PBW, ordered with $F$ first, gives the basis of the localized quotient with $F$-powers $-1,-2,\ldots$; reflection permutes the remaining positive roots. Hence the displayed vector generates the quotient. Its character is $s(e^\eta\sum_{r\ge1}e^{r\alpha_i}\prod_{\beta>0,\beta\ne\alpha_i}(1-e^{-\beta})^{-1})=\operatorname{ch}\Delta_{s\cdot\eta}$. The highest-vector surjection is an isomorphism by equality of each finite weight dimension. This fixes its scalar by $v_{s\cdot\eta}\mapsto[F^{-1}v_\eta]$. [F2, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 For finite-dimensional $X$, localization commutes with tensoring. On $M_F\otimes X$ the total operator $F_M+F_X$ has inverse $F_M^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}(-F_M^{-1}F_X)^k$; the sum is finite since $F_X$ is nilpotent. The localization universal property identifies $(M\otimes X)_F$ with $M_F\otimes X$ and identifies the embedded $M\otimes X$. Quotienting and the Weyl matrix $W_X=\exp(E_X)\exp(-F_X)\exp(E_X)$ identify $T_s(M\otimes X)$ naturally with $T_s(M)\otimes X$. For two finite tensor factors, $W_{X\otimes Y}=W_X\otimes W_Y$, so associativity and the tensor-unit diagrams commute. The diagonal Weyl action fixes the invariant Casimir and commutes with flips, proving their compatibility as actual operators. [step 2.1, construct, algebra, step 3.1]

5.1 Choose regular coset-dominant $\lambda$ in the weight-coset category. Crossing distinct cosets preserves each coset's internal order, so $s\cdot\lambda$ meets the same regular coset-dominance hypotheses; its central character equals $\chi_\lambda$. For a generator map encoded by $t\in(E^*\otimes F\otimes U_\chi)^{\mathfrak g}$, its action is the finite sum of finite-tensor matrix entries followed by enveloping operators on $\Delta_\lambda$. The invariant matrix map commutes with the total $F$ on the tensor modules, so its unique localized extension agrees with the same enveloping-operator formula under the tensor localization of step 4.1. Passing to the quotient, twisting and applying the matrices of step 4.1 transforms $t$ by simultaneous Weyl conjugation in its three factors. Each $t$ lies in a finite adjoint submodule, so that conjugation is $\exp(E_{\mathrm{diag}})\exp(-F_{\mathrm{diag}})\exp(E_{\mathrm{diag}})$ and fixes $t$, since its diagonal $\mathfrak g$-action is zero. Thus $T_s$ induces exactly the common Hom identification of [F1], respecting composition and identity. The scalar from step 3.1 is the same on all generators $X\otimes\Delta_\lambda$, so it cancels on every generator Hom space; an arbitrary unnormalized scalar is not treated as a literal equality of highest vectors. [F1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Every object has a finite presentation by finite direct sums and summands of the generators in [F1]. Exactness and steps 3.1–4.1 show that its $T_s$ image is the cokernel of a map between target generators, hence belongs to the target category $\mathcal O$. Step 5.1 identifies all generator maps. Every target presentation therefore lifts, proving essential surjectivity. Applying Hom from a generator to a source presentation and its target presentation gives identical cokernel diagrams, since those generators are projective; applying Hom from a presented object gives identical kernel diagrams. This proves full faithfulness on all objects. Idempotents are preserved and reflected by the generator Hom identification, so summands cause no gap. Consequently $T_s$ is an exact category equivalence, established on actual maps and presentations. [F1, F2, F5, step 2.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 Compose these swaps in a stable bubble sort by the fixed coset order. Each swap crosses different cosets; none permutes indices inside a coset. The composite sends $\Delta_\eta$ to $\Delta_{w\cdot\eta}$ and therefore sends its unique simple head to $L(w\cdot\eta)$. It transports projective covers by exact equivalence and essentiality. Every original column consists entirely of one coset; stable sorting retains its coordinates as a consecutive block and retains their internal order. At the end, the original Levi simple roots are therefore positive simple roots of the sorted column Levi. Their highest-weight integral-dominance pairings are unchanged. By the actual Levi simple criterion and Serre property of [F4], the composite and its inverse restrict to the full parabolic subcategories. Because generalized Vermas are the largest parabolic-finite quotients of ordinary Vermas, their quotient universal property is transported, giving the claimed generalized-standard labels as modules. No intermediate swap is asserted to preserve an intermediate parabolic subcategory. [F4, step 3.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra]

8.1 The coherent comparison of two sorting paths can be made on tensor-projective generators. Each path has the common [F1] Hom matrix identification of step 5.1; their final Weyl representatives differ at most by a diagonal torus matrix when they induce the same coordinate permutation. Diagonal simultaneous action again fixes invariant matrices. Their reference-standard highest lines admit a unique comparison after fixing its nonzero scalar; tensor it with $X$ for every generator and summand. The equality on generator Hom matrices makes these comparisons natural, and taking presentation cokernels extends them uniquely to all objects, independently of a presentation by full faithfulness. Comparisons for three paths compose because they coincide on the normalized reference generator and its tensor presentations. This proves the stated normalization and coherence, without asserting an unnormalized inverse-twist or braid identity. [F1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, construct, algebra, step 7.1]

9.1 After sorting let $\mathfrak q$ have contiguous coset Levi $\mathfrak l=\bigoplus_\kappa\mathfrak{gl}_{N_\kappa}$ and positive outside radical $\mathfrak u$. In a fixed linkage block $C$, [F3] says exactly that highest labels are obtained by permutations within the coset blocks, including when entries repeat. Hence all highest labels have the same block-centre values $z_\kappa$. For each initial union of coset blocks, write $Z_r$ for its diagonal trace and $b_r$ for the common highest-label value. Every module weight satisfies $b_r-\mu(Z_r)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$: this holds on simple highest-weight modules by their negative-root weights and on all finite-length objects by their composition series. An outside negative root strictly lowers at least one prefix; an inside root leaves every prefix fixed. The simultaneous top section $S(M)=\{v:Z_rv=b_rv\ \forall r\}$ is therefore a Levi module and is annihilated by $\mathfrak u$. It is exact, since it is a direct sum of Cartan weight spaces and the Cartan acts semisimply. These are integer differences from fixed complex values, not inequalities on complex numbers. [F2, F3, construct, algebra, step 8.1]

10.1 In fact $M^{\mathfrak u}=S(M)$. If a nonzero homogeneous radical-invariant vector lies in a lower prefix section, its Levi cyclic module has a highest vector: its positive Levi orbit is finite-dimensional and a maximal weight therein is killed by every positive Levi root. Radical invariants are Levi-stable because $[\mathfrak l,\mathfrak u]\subset\mathfrak u$. That Levi highest vector is thus a full $\mathfrak g$ highest vector. Its cyclic module has a simple highest-weight quotient of the same weight and the same strictly lower prefix, contradicting the actual label restriction in [F3]. Decomposing a general invariant into centre weights gives the same contradiction componentwise. Moreover $S$ detects nonzero objects: every simple of $C$ has a nonzero highest vector in its top section, and exactness plus a composition series proves the assertion for every nonzero finite-length object. [F2, F3, step 9.1, algebra]

11.1 Let $C_{\mathfrak l}$ be the product integral-reflection orbit for the Levi highest weights with these fixed scalar centres, and define $R(X)=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak q)}X$, with $\mathfrak u$ acting by zero. PBW makes $R$ exact and identifies $S(R(X))=X$ naturally: every outside negative PBW monomial lowers some prefix, so only its degree-zero term contributes. For a Levi simple $L_{\mathfrak l}(\eta)$, induction is a quotient of the ordinary $\mathfrak g$ Verma of label $\eta$, hence lies in $C$ by [F3] and has finite length by [F2]. Every composition factor has nonzero top section by step 10.1; exactness and $S(R(L_{\mathfrak l}(\eta)))=L_{\mathfrak l}(\eta)$ imply that there is only one factor. Thus $R(L_{\mathfrak l}(\eta))=L_{\mathfrak g}(\eta)$ is simple. Exactness extends block membership and finite length to $R(X)$ for every finite-length $X$ by a Levi composition series. [F2, F3, step 9.1, step 10.1, construct, algebra]

12.1 Induction and radical invariants are adjoint, and step 10.1 identifies the latter with $S$. Their unit is PBW's top-section isomorphism $X\to S(R(X))$. For the counit $R(S(M))\to M$, applying exact $S$ gives this identity, so its kernel and cokernel have zero top section; both are finite-length objects of $C$ and vanish by detection in step 10.1. Hence $R$ and $S$ are inverse exact category equivalences. This argument proves full faithfulness from the actual unit and counit. It does not deduce it from composition matrices. By induction transitivity, ordinary Levi Vermas go to ordinary $\mathfrak g$ Vermas; the corresponding column-generalized Vermas go to their genuine column-parabolic inductions. The Levi integrability criterion restricts the equivalence to the column-parabolic subcategories just as in step 7.1; projective covers again follow by exact equivalence. [F4, step 10.1, step 11.1, construct, algebra]

13.1 Each finite Levi factor block has a finite projective generator (finite label orbit and [F2], or its parabolic reflector). For two outer tensor projectives, their Hom is the tensor product of their factor Homs, by tensor-Hom and the finite-dimensional factor Hom spaces; applying a factor-projective Hom successively is exact: a fixed weight for the other factors cuts a finite-generated factor-$\mathcal O$ module, since PBW bounds the negative monomials in those fixed coordinates; factor projectivity therefore applies weight by weight. The resulting multiplicity module is in the remaining factor $\mathcal O$, by the same PBW finiteness with the finitely many generator weights of the projective. Their outer tensor sum therefore is projective, and its simple quotients cover all factor tuples. Those tuples exhaust the simple labels of the direct-sum Lie algebra: the outer tensor of the factor simples is cyclic on the tensor of their highest vectors. Any nonzero submodule has a highest vector by positive-root local finiteness and bounded highest-weight support; taking invariants successively in the separate positive root algebras leaves only that tensor highest line, because a simple highest-weight factor has no other highest vector. The submodule thus contains the cyclic generator, proving simplicity and identifying the unique simple quotient of the direct-sum Verma. Thus the outer tensor generator gives finite presentations of every object and has the tensor-product endomorphism algebra. Applying the generator Hom and its presentation inverse proves the product description in the Statement. This also proves standard/simple/projective tensor labels as objects, not just as classes. [F2, F4, step 12.1, construct, algebra]

14.1 The original tableau convention gives $\eta_i+\rho_i=a_i+(N-1)/2$, so dot sorting is literally stable sorting of the $a_i$. In the sorted $\kappa$ block the Levi coordinate is $a_t+B_\kappa+t-1$. The integral coordinate from the Statement is $a_t-c_\kappa+n-n_\kappa+t-1$; their difference is exactly $\delta_\kappa$. Tensoring with the one-dimensional Lie algebra representation $x\mapsto\delta_\kappa\operatorname{tr}(x)$ is an exact inverse equivalence with inverse shift $-\delta_\kappa$, and its tensor associativity is ordinary scalar multiplication. It carries highest vectors, induced standards, simple heads and projective covers. Since a ground entry in global row $r$ is $c_\kappa+1-r$, its integral image is $1-(r-n+n_\kappa)$; these are the actual bottom-aligned integral ground rows. The retained heights give $m_j=q_j-n_\kappa$ nonincreasing and $m_j+1-(1-n_\kappa)=q_j$. For an admitted-ground label, subtracting its original ground entry gives a nonnegative integer; the displayed dictionary preserves that difference. Its integral entry is therefore at least the corresponding bottom-aligned integral ground entry and lies in the fixed admitted alphabet of [F4]. For an arbitrary genuine label the scalar shift still gives an integral parabolic highest weight, but no fixed-cut membership follows. Thus the height/charge dictionary holds generally and the fixed admitted component hypotheses of [F4] hold on the stated admitted-ground subcategories, without treating a nonintegral scalar trace character as an algebraic determinant character. [F4, step 7.1, step 13.1, construct, algebra]

15.1 For clarity about tensor transport, the ordinary induction tensor identity is $R(X)\otimes V\cong U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak q)}(X\otimes\operatorname{Res}_{\mathfrak q}V)$; it follows from the coproduct and antipode and is natural in $X,V$. The restricted vector representation has its actual prefix-$\mathfrak q$ filtration whose sections are the coset vector modules $V_\kappa$ with outside radical zero. Exact induction therefore gives a filtration of $R(X)\otimes V$ with sections $R(X\otimes V_\kappa)$. A projected linkage/entry-multiset tensor summand admitting an entry change in coset $\kappa$ kills the other sections: their highest labels change a different coset multiset, so their central characters or linkage classes differ by [F3]. Only the $\kappa$ section survives, giving its natural component comparison; the dual vector representation has the reversed filtration and the same argument. Thus the residue-projected operators transport to the appropriate integral factor. Iterated tensor comparisons use the same actual filtrations and the associative tensor identity, so their diagrams commute; no unrestricted tensor-product assertion is inferred. [F3, step 11.1, step 12.1, construct, algebra, step 14.1]

16.1 The trace-character shift changes the relevant vector Casimir eigenvalue by its scalar: for $\Omega=\sum_{i,j}E_{ij}\otimes E_{ji}$, replacing the first-factor action by $E_{ij}+\delta_{ij}\delta$ adds $\delta\sum_i1\otimes E_{ii}=\delta$ on a vector representation; the dual gives the corresponding opposite shift. The offset can be computed explicitly: on a vector-tensor Verma section of highest label $\eta+\varepsilon_i$, the quadratic central element has value $\sum_k\eta_k(\eta_k+N+1-2k)$, while its value on the vector is $N$. Taking half the difference gives the global tensor-Casimir eigenvalue $\eta_i+1-i$. For the Levi coordinate $t=i-B_\kappa$, the same calculation gives $\eta_i+1-t$, greater by $B_\kappa$. Hence the trace shift contributes $\delta_\kappa-B_\kappa=c_\kappa-n+n_\kappa$ to the original residue: $(c_\kappa+q_j-n)-(q_j-n_\kappa)=c_\kappa-n+n_\kappa$. This computes the parameter dictionary and the block projections of step 15.1; no integer residue is silently equated with its complex original. It does not replace a proof of the full affine-Hecke natural-transformation presentation. Together with steps 4.1 and 15.1 this proves the claimed normalized compatibility, and steps 7.1, 12.1–13.1 and 14.1 prove the typed category equivalence with all stated labels and hypotheses. [step 4.1, step 7.1, step 12.1, step 13.1, step 14.1, step 15.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: The Whittaker functor from the relevant parabolic category-O summand
items.statement:
Work over $\mathbb C$ and assume the Axiom of Choice where projective covers,
duality and locally unital assemblies enter. Let
$\lambda=(0\le p_1\le\cdots\le p_n)$ be a pyramid with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, let $c=(c_1,\dots,c_l)$ be admissible in the sense that
$c_i-c_j\in\mathbb Z$ implies $c_i=c_j$, and let
$\mathcal O_c^d$ be the relevant summand of the genuine parabolic
category $\mathcal O$ attached to the labels $c$ and the degree $d$: its
objects are the modules whose column-strict labels have nonnegative integral
differences from the ground entries of each column, i.e. the labels with
$\Lambda$-diagram content $c_j+q_j-n$ in the sense of
[[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]] (the ambient categories are the
ones of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
and [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]).

For a $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated object $N$ of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$, the **Whittaker functor** is the covariant finite-dimensional dual
$$V(N):=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak m}(N,\mathbb C_\chi)^*.$$
Its $W(\lambda)$ action is obtained from the continuous $\chi$-part of the right
linear dual, then the reflected head/tail identification proved below. In the
notation $D_{\mathrm{row}}\mathrm{Wh}D_{\mathrm{row}}$, the middle Whittaker
operation is performed on this continuous $\chi$-part, not on the uncompleted
ordinary row-restricted dual. Write $N(A)$ for source standard objects,
$L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ for source simples, and $L_W(A)$ for the resulting
nonzero simple $W$-modules. These namespaces are distinct.

The verification below records the properties used on this page: $V$ is exact
on the $U(\mathfrak m)$-finitely-generated objects of genuine parabolic
$\mathcal O$ and intertwines finite tensoring, the Casimir and the flips; $V$
is distinct from the Hecke quotient $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$
constructed later; for the ground simple projective-injective $P_c$ and
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ one has $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and
$V(T)=V_c^{\otimes d}$; and $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))$ is the simple $W$-module $L_W(A)$ for
standard labels $A$ and zero otherwise. Nonintegral origins use the typed
equivalence of the all-weight Harish-Chandra comparison of the source; no
arbitrary complex $c$ is identified with an integral block. After fixing the
ground identification $i_0\colon V(P_c)\to\mathbb C_c$, the compatible functor
and the maps $j_d$ are unique up to the normalized unique natural isomorphism;
without this normalization scalar automorphisms prevent literal uniqueness.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** Assume AC. Use $U=U(\mathfrak m)$ and $I=I_\chi$. The source standards are $N(A)$, source simples $L_{\mathcal O}(A)$ (abbreviated $L_O(A)$ in the computations), and output simples $L_W(A)$. The finite tensor/Hopf comparisons use the actual Skryabin displayed map, not cofree constant evaluation.

1.1 Let U=U(m), I=I_chi. Replace x by y=x−chi(x). These shifted generators have the original brackets, because chi vanishes on brackets. Choose a basis adapted to the lower-central filtration, with weight w_i the largest lower-central index containing its basis vector. PBW reordering and the commutator formula show that I^n is spanned by ordered monomials of total lower-central weight≥n: one inclusion follows from reordering n factors, while the reverse follows because each basis vector of weight w lies in I^w, being a linear combination of iterated brackets of length w. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.2 The Rees algebra R=⊕_(n≥0) I^n t^n is generated by y_i t^r, 0≤r≤w_i. Their span is a finite-dimensional Lie algebra: a nonzero bracket component y_k has w_k≥w_i+w_j, so r+s≤w_k. PBW gives its enveloping algebra a polynomial associated graded. For any left ideal, Hilbert basis gives finitely many generators of its homogeneous leading ideal; lift them and subtract matching highest-degree terms until the nonnegative degree decreases to zero. The lifts generate the original ideal. Thus the enveloping algebra is left noetherian, and its surjection onto R makes R left noetherian. For a left ideal J⊂U, ⊕(J∩I^n)t^n is a graded left ideal of R and has finitely many homogeneous generators. For fixed k, choosing n greater than k plus their largest degrees gives J∩I^n⊂I^k J. This is the precise Artin–Rees consequence needed here. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.3 Set E_chi=∪_(n≥0)(U/I^n)^*, with left action (x f)(r)=f(r x). To prove injectivity, take a U-linear map phi:J→E_chi. U is noetherian, so choose finitely many generators of J. A common I^k kills their images and hence all images, since I is two-sided. The scalar functional lambda(j)=phi(j)(1) kills I^k J. Choose n with J∩I^n⊂I^k J, extend lambda from J/(J∩I^n) to U/I^n, and call the extension a∈E_chi. The map U→E_chi, u↦u a, extends phi, because at r its value on j is a(rj)=phi(rj)(1)=phi(j)(r). Baer's criterion gives injectivity. This supplies the injective-continuous-dual assertion cited without proof in BK Lemma8.20. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.4 For a U(m)-finitely generated g-module X, evaluation at1 identifies Hom_m(X,E_chi) with the scalar functionals lambda:X→C that kill I^n X for some n. Indeed, reconstruct the map by F_lambda(v)(r)=lambda(rv); finitely many generators give a common n. The right U(g)-action is (lambda·u)(v)=lambda(uv). On E-valued maps its formula is therefore [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.5 (F·u)(v)(r)=lambda(u r v), [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.6 not the generally non-m-linear expression F(uv)(r)=lambda(r u v). This distinguishes the compressed scalar-functional notation in the source from a literal E-valued composition. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.7 The right action preserves continuity. For a fixed u∈U(g), the finite PBW subspace generated by all iterated ad m on u is finite-dimensional and its negative-column action is nilpotent; sufficiently long products of ad m vanish. Moving u past a product of sufficiently many shifted m generators therefore leaves at least n of them on the left. Equivalently u I^(n+C)⊂I^n U(g) for some C=C(u). Thus lambda u kills I^(n+C)X. On this continuous-dual module the right shifted m-action is locally nilpotent. Injectivity of E_chi makes Hom_m(−,E_chi) exact, and right Skryabin makes its Whittaker vectors exact. These Whittaker vectors are precisely Hom_m(X,C_chi). Dualizing this finite-dimensional vector space gives an exact covariant functor. [F1, F2, F5, construct, algebra]

1.8 The restricted dual uses the row-sum torus a=span{Σ_(row(j)=r)E_jj}, not the full Cartan and not the column-origin vector c. Every e-adjacent pair lies in one row, so chi has a-weight0. If X is generated over U(m) by finitely many a-weight spaces, an m-linear functional into C_chi vanishes outside those finitely many weights: lambda(uv)=chi(u)lambda(v), and chi(u)=0 in every nonzero a-weight. Thus the restricted-dual definition agrees with the entire finite-dimensional Hom space. Hence the source action factors through the genuine cyclotomic algebra, not only its $V$ image. Step 7.1 transports it to $M=V_c^{\otimes d}$ as the actual $(W,H_d)$ bimodule action. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 6.1, step 7.1, construct, algebra]

8.2 $V$ maps $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}$ into $\operatorname{End}_{W}(M)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$ by step 2.5, and its image contains $B$ because every target Hecke operator is the transport of its actual source Casimir/place operator. A nonzero source endomorphism has a nonzero image $X\subseteq T$. Step 3.3 proves $V(X)\ne0$, and exactness identifies $V(X)$ with the image of its transported endomorphism. Hence the endomorphism map is injective as well as surjective, giving $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B$. Detection uses the standard-label SOCLE criterion, never a claim that all composition factors of $T$ are standard. [F1, F2, F3, F7, step 7.1, step 3.3, step 2.5, construct, algebra]

9.1 Choose a full finite projective generator Q of the genuine O summand containing T as an explicit summand and write its algebra as A; the projector onto T is e and B=eAe. The exact Schur functor is e(−). It kills precisely the offStd simples. Its left adjoint Ae⊗_B− is right exact and satisfies e(Ae⊗X)=X. The counit Ae⊗eN→N has kernel and cokernel killed by e. Applying V sends it to an isomorphism. Therefore V factors through e(−), and its factor F on B-mod is naturally M⊗_B− by finite free presentations. This factor is exact: the only failure of exactness after the left adjoint is killed by e and hence by Wh. It is faithful, since every B-simple is eL_O(A) for a Std label and its V image is nonzero; exactness then detects every nonzero image of a morphism. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F7, step 1.18, step 3.3, step 8.2, construct, algebra]

10.1 A finite-dimensional right B-module whose tensor functor is exact is projective. Explicitly, take its finite projective cover P→M with kernel K⊂P rad B. Tensor the inclusion K→P with B/rad B; flatness makes K/K rad B inject into P/P rad B, but this map is zero, so Nakayama gives K=0. Faithfulness forces every right indecomposable projective to occur in M: otherwise tensor with the corresponding left simple would vanish. Thus M_B is a progenerator. The first independently proved raw centralizer identity in step 2.5 gives Wd=End_B(M). The usual generator presentation/evaluation argument now gives the genuine Morita equivalence Wd-mod≃B-mod. In particular F sends B-simples to Wd-simples, proving the full relevant V simple-image claim without assuming it earlier. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F8, step 2.5, step 9.1, construct, algebra]

11.1 Tensor compatibility and the actual Casimir/flip intertwiners are proved in steps 1.9–1.18, using the original head/right normalizer and the actual balanced Skryabin map. Thus $V(P_c)=\mathbb C_c$ and $V(P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d})=V_c^{\otimes d}$. The preceding kernel/Morita construction proves $V(L_{\mathcal O}(A))=L_W(A)$ for standard labels and zero otherwise; it never asserts that the image of a source standard $N(A)$ is simple. The normalized comparison is determined on the ground and its tensor words, hence on the detecting tensor bimodule and on finite free quotient presentations through the established exact Morita factorization. Its ground normalization removes scalar ambiguity. This proves the stated properties of the genuine Whittaker functor, while keeping it distinct from the Hecke Hom quotient. [F1, F2, F3, F4, choose, construct, algebra] ∎
