items.title: The higher-level Schur-Weyl double centralizer and Schur quotient
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix the pyramid $\lambda$ with columns
$q_1\ge\cdots\ge q_l$, an origin $c$, a degree $d\ge0$, and let
$V_c^{\otimes d}$ be the truncated tensor space with its finite W-algebra image
$W_d$ and cyclotomic Hecke image $B_d$. Then:

1. $W_d$ and $B_d$ are mutual centralizers on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, for every
   complex origin $c$; this is the raw double centralizer.
2. For admissible origins, $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a progenerator and
   $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence between
   $W_d$-mod and $B_d$-mod.
3. The genuine Whittaker functor followed by this equivalence is the exact
   Schur Serre quotient killing exactly the off-standard simples; it is fully
   faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all
   tiltings, and its left adjoint is right exact and recovers
   $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but need not recover every projective.
4. For a nonempty pyramid, in the stable range $q_l\ge d$ the algebra $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic
   algebra $H_d(\mathbf a)$; outside the stable range and for admissible
   origins the central-corner identification $B_d=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ is used.

Mutual centralizers alone do not give the Morita statement: the nonadmissible
origin example with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$ and $d=2$ has a nonprojective tensor
module while the mutual centralizer identities still hold.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The pyramid, the origin $c$, the tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$, the image algebras $W_d$, $B_d$, and the tensor object $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ of the relevant parabolic summand.

[F1] The raw filtered double centralizer holds for every complex origin; for admissible origins the tensor space is a progenerator and $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence $W_d\text{-mod}\to B_d\text{-mod}$; the nonadmissible counterexample with $c=(0,1)$, $q=(1,1)$, $d=2$ separates the two assertions ([[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]]).

[F2] $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_d$ and, componentwise, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(T_\alpha)^{\mathrm{op}}=B_\alpha$ for admissible origins; the map $H_d(\mathbf a)\twoheadrightarrow B_d$ is surjective with injectivity exactly in the nonempty stable range and also in the trivial empty branch ([[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]]).

[F3] The Whittaker quotient $\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ is exact, its kernel is the Serre subcategory of off-standard simples, it is fully faithful on all projectives and on tiltings, its left adjoint $\pi^*=T\otimes_{B_d}-$ is right exact, and $\pi^*\pi$ recovers $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but need not recover every projective of the ambient category ([[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]], [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]]).

[F4] The stable range is $q_l\ge d$; in it $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$, and outside it the admissible-origin image is the central block corner $fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ ([[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], [[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The mutual centralizer and Morita inputs of [F1], the endomorphism isomorphism of [F2], the Schur quotient properties of [F3], and the stable-range/corner dictionary of [F4].

1.1 The raw double centralizer. For arbitrary complex origin the filtered leading-symbol lifting argument of [F1] gives $W_d=B_d'$ and $B_d=W_d'$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$, with associated graded images the Vust centralizers; this is the all-origin clause and does not use admissibility. [F1, algebra]

1.2 Admissible Morita equivalence. Assume $c$ admissible. By the progenerator clause of [F1], $V_c^{\otimes d}$ is a progenerator for $W_d$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},-)$ is a Morita equivalence; by the component clause of [F2] its endomorphism algebra is $B_d=\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$, so the equivalence is the standard one attached to the $(W_d,B_d)$-bimodule $V_c^{\otimes d}$, identifying $W_d$-mod with $B_d$-mod. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The Schur Serre quotient. The composite of the genuine Whittaker functor with the equivalence of step 1.2 is $\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ by [F2] and [F3]; it is exact and its kernel is the Serre subcategory generated by the off-standard simples, so it is the exact Schur Serre quotient killing exactly those simples. [F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Full faithfulness and the left adjoint. By [F3] the quotient is fully faithful on all projectives of the relevant parabolic summand and on all tiltings, while its left adjoint $T\otimes_{B_d}-$ is only right exact and $\pi^*\pi$ recovers $\operatorname{add}(T)$ but need not recover every projective; these boundaries are part of the statement and are not repaired by changing conventions. [F3, step 2.1, given]

4.1 Stable range and central corner. For the empty pyramid degree zero is the scalar identity and positive degree is the zero-algebra identity, so all comparisons hold directly with $f=1$ in degree zero and $f=0$ in positive degree. For a nonempty pyramid, if $q_l\ge d$ then $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ by [F4] and the component form of step 2.1 uses the full cyclotomic algebra; outside the stable range, and for admissible origins, the image is the central block corner $B_d=fH_d(\mathbf a)f$ of [F4], with the component corners $B_\alpha=f_\alpha H_\alpha(\mathbf a)f_\alpha$ of [F2]. For nonadmissible origins only the raw mutual centralizer statement of step 1.1 remains. [F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The statement separates three levels of structure that are often conflated: the all-origin mutual centralizer (step 1.1), the admissible-origin Morita equivalence (step 1.2), and the stable-range simplification $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ (step 4.1). Each consumes a different supplier.
- The left adjoint $\pi^*$ is used only where it is exact enough: recovering $\operatorname{add}(T)$ on standard-labelled prinjectives, never for arbitrary projectives.

items.title: Schur functor images of standard, simple, projective and tilting objects
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$. Let
$\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ be the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
$T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$. Use the current category-O namespace:
$N(A):=M(A)$ is the generalized standard, $K(A):=\nabla(A)$ the costandard,
$L(A)$ the category-O simple and $P(A)$ its projective cover, as in
[[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]].
The source17 symbol $K(A)$ denotes our $L(A)$, not our costandard $K(A)$.
Write $\mathsf L(A):=\mathrm{Wh}(L(A))$ for the finite-W image of the
category-O simple; for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ this is the source finite-W simple
appearing in the Whittaker/Morita contract of
[[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]].
In particular the $W_d$-Hom below takes a finite-W module as its second
argument. Let $\mathrm{Std}$ be the standard labels. Then:

1. For every label $A$, the Schur image of the standard object $N(A)$ is the
   intrinsic affine-induced Specht module
   $$S(A)=H_d\otimes_{H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}}\Bigl(\bigotimes_j \mathrm{ev}^*_{a_j}S^{\mu^{(j)}}\Bigr),\qquad a_j=c_j+q_j-n,$$
   where $\mu^{(j)}$ is the partition of $d_j$ read from the nonnegative
   ground differences in the $j$-th column of $A$ and the factors are induced
   along the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1,\dots,d_l}=H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots
   \otimes H_{d_l}$. Its affine action factors through the cyclotomic image $B_d$, so the same module is obtained by replacing $H_d$ in this tensor product by $H_d(\mathbf a)$.
2. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$ the module
   $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is
   simple, the modules $D(A)$, $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, form a complete set of
   pairwise non-isomorphic simples of the Hecke image $B_d$, and
   $\pi(L(A))=0$ for $A\notin\mathrm{Std}$.
3. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, $\pi(P(A))$ is the projective cover $Y(A)$ of
   $D(A)$, and $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$; ambient off-standard projectives
   still have their genuine images, and no projective-preservation assertion
   is made for them.
4. Images of tiltings carry the opposite-parabolic standard/Specht flag
   coefficients, and $\pi$ is fully faithful on tiltings.
5. For $A\in\mathrm{Col}$ and $B\in\mathrm{Std}$,
   $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$, where $d_{B,A}$ is the typed
   canonical-basis coefficient of the Fock-space dictionary; for $B\notin
   \mathrm{Std}$ the symbol $D(B)$ is not a Hecke simple. All interfaces are
   ungraded at parameter $1$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The admissible origin $c$, the tensor object $T=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$, the Schur functor $\pi$, the standard and costandard objects $N(A),K(A)$, the simples $L(A)$, the projectives $P(A)$, and the Hecke image $B_d$.

[F1] In the actual category-O namespace the generalized standards are $M(A)=N(A)$, the simples are $L(A)$, projective covers are $P(A)$ and costandards are $\nabla(A)=K(A)$. These have the BGG reciprocity and standard/costandard/tilting flags of [[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]], [[def-standard-costandard-filtered-and-tilting-objects-in-a-highest-weight-category]] and [[thm-indecomposable-tiltings-exist-and-are-classified-in-parabolic-category-o]]. Composition multiplicities below are always taken against the simple $L(B)$; they are not standard-flag multiplicities against a costandard.

[F2] The Schur functor $\pi$ is exact, kills exactly the off-standard simples, recovers $\operatorname{add}(T)$ under $\pi^*\pi$, and is fully faithful on all projectives and on all tiltings; $T$ contains every standard-labelled projective-injective cover ([[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]], [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]]).

[F3] The filtered double centralizer identifies $B_d=\operatorname{End}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d})^{\mathrm{op}}$, and the Schur quotient is the composite of the genuine Whittaker functor with the Morita equivalence; the stable range gives $B_d=H_d(\mathbf a)$ ([[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-double-centralizer]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]], [[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]], [[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]).

[F4] The Fock-space dictionary: the canonical, dual-canonical and quasi-canonical bases of the higher-level Fock module carry the typed labels of simples, projectives and tiltings of the summand, and the coefficient $d_{B,A}(1)$ computes the corresponding multiplicity at parameter $1$ ([[def-dual-canonical-canonical-and-quasi-canonical-fock-bases]], [[thm-simples-projectives-and-tiltings-map-to-the-three-distinguished-fock-bases]]).

[F5] The cyclotomic Hecke algebra has the bounded monomial basis and the affine evaluation homomorphisms $\mathrm{ev}_{a}\colon H_{d_j}\to\mathbb C[S_{d_j}]$, $x_k\mapsto a+\sum_{h<k}(h,k)$ ([[def-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-algebra]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The standard $N(A)$, the costandard $K(A)$, the labels of $\mathrm{Std}$, and the corner data of the stable realization. For the empty pyramid, degree zero has the sole empty label and all its modules and functors are $\mathbb C$ and the identity; positive degree has no labels and only zero modules. The assertions follow directly there, and the following construction treats a nonempty pyramid.

1.1 **A regular corner in the stable realization.** Add full ground rows until there are $d$ distinct rows of length $l$, and choose one rightmost box in each such row; let $v_S$ be their ordered tensor and $e_S$ the row-weight projection onto tensors using these rows once each. The actual tensor matrices in [F3] preserve row multisets, so this projection commutes with the right Hecke action and belongs to the left image by the first centralizer. The vectors $v_Sx_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}w$, $0\le r_i<l$, $w\in S_d$, have distinct leading tensors: the leading dot moves its box one column left, while a permutation changes the ordered distinct rows. They therefore form a basis of $e_SU$ by triangularity, and its cardinality is $l^dd!$. Thus $b\mapsto v_Sb$ identifies $e_SU$ with the right regular $H_d(\mathbf a)$-module. Put $A=\operatorname{End}_{H_d(\mathbf a)}U$. Since $e_SU$ is regular, $Ae_S=\operatorname{Hom}_{H_d}(e_SU,U)\cong U$ by evaluation at $v_S$. Consequently $h:H_d(\mathbf a)\to e_SAe_S$, characterized by $h(b)v_S=v_Sb$, is an algebra isomorphism, and $\theta\mapsto\theta(v_S)$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{A}(U,M)$ with $e_SM$ for every finite-image module $M$. The left Hecke action on this corner is $h$, not the naive right action on $M$. [F3, F5, construct, algebra]

2.1 **The cyclic symmetric generator and its bottom quotient.** Write $A-A_c=(a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ and form the actual cumulative-column $\mathfrak p$-module $Z=\bigotimes_i\operatorname{Sym}^{a_i}(V_{\le\operatorname{col}(i)})$. Its bottom column degree is $b=\sum_i a_i(l-\operatorname{col}(i))$; the higher-degree part is a $\mathfrak p$-submodule, and $Z/Z_{>b}$ is the inflated Levi module $Z_b=\bigotimes_j\bigotimes_r\operatorname{Sym}^{\mu_r^{(j)}}(E_j)$. Put $w_A=\sum_{w\in\prod_iS_{a_i}}w$ and $x_A=\prod_i\prod_{k=1}^{a_i}\prod_{j>\operatorname{col}(i)}(x_{a_1+\cdots+a_{i-1}+k}-a_j)$. Apply these factors in order starting with the first tensor place. The actual dot formula gives $v_Sx_A=v_{\mathbf j}$, where $\mathbf j$ has the ordered rows of $v_S$ and column sequence prescribed by $A-A_c$; subtracting $a_j$ cancels the scalar at column $j$ and moves that box one column left. Hence $v_Sx_Aw_A=v_{\mathbf j}w_A\in e_SZ$. More generally the vectors $v_Swx_1^{r_1}\cdots x_d^{r_d}x_Aw_A$, with $0\le r_k<\operatorname{col}(\mathbf j_k)$ and $w$ ranging over cosets of $\prod_i S_{a_i}$, have distinct leading symmetrized tensors and span $e_SZ$ by the ordinary symmetric-tensor basis. Thus this vector generates $e_SZ$ as a corner module, and its image generates $e_S(Z/Z_{>b})$. These are actual vector identities and triangular basis statements, rather than a character identification. [F1, F3, F5, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 **The affine colour fibre.** Ordinary Levi Schur-Weyl gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak h}(U,Z_b)\cong\bigotimes_j M^{\mu^{(j)}}$ on the canonical colour fibre, where $M^{\mu}$ is the symmetric-group permutation module. Its vectors in the corner are $v_{\mathbf j}ww_A+e_SZ_{>b}$ with $w\in S_{d_1}\times\cdots\times S_{d_l}$. For $k=d_1+\cdots+d_{j-1}+1$, the identity $v_{\mathbf j}=v_Sx_A$ and commutativity of dots give $h(x_k)v_{\mathbf j}ww_A=v_Sx_Ax_kww_A=v_{\mathbf j}x_kww_A$. In the bottom quotient the dot formula has scalar $a_j=c_j+q_j-n$: its left-neighbour term has higher degree, all preceding places have strictly smaller column and all later places have greater or equal column, so both signed transposition sums are empty. Thus $x_k$ acts as $a_j$ on that canonical fibre. The affine cross relations then determine the remaining dots as $a_j$ plus their within-block Jucys-Murphy sums. This proves that the fibre inclusion is a homomorphism for the affine Young subalgebra $H_{d_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{d_l}$, with module $\bigotimes_j\mathrm{ev}_{a_j}^*M^{\mu^{(j)}}$, and its image generates the entire corner by step 2.1. [F3, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 **The genuine Specht isomorphism.** The Levi Young-symmetrizer map gives an actual quotient $Z_b\twoheadrightarrow V(A)$ and hence a $\mathfrak p$-quotient $Z/Z_{>b}\twoheadrightarrow V(A)$. The canonical colour fibre quotient is $\bigotimes_j S^{\mu^{(j)}}$, by ordinary Levi Schur-Weyl. The affine fibre map in step 3.1 descends through this actual quotient and still generates: $e_S$ is exact and the generating vector of its source maps onto a generator of its quotient. Affine induction therefore gives a surjection $S(A)\twoheadrightarrow e_SV(A)$. The multilinear row-weight part of $\bigotimes_j S_{\mu^{(j)}}(E_j)$ has one summand for each allocation of the $d$ distinct rows into ordered colour subsets of sizes $d_j$, and on each subset its weight space is the polytabloid Specht space. Its dimension is $d!/(d_1!\cdots d_l!)\prod_j\dim S^{\mu^{(j)}}$. This is also the induced module's dimension, since the affine algebra is free over its affine Young subalgebra with the finite shuffle basis. The existing surjection is therefore an isomorphism. Steps 1.1 and [F2] identify its target with $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,V(A))=\pi(N(A))$, preserving the actual Hecke maps. [F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 **Descent to the original pyramid.** Extend the original label $A$ by the added ground rows, producing a contractible large label $A^+$. Its column partitions $\mu^{(j)}$ and roots $a_j$ are unchanged. The actual original-path/zero-occupancy compression in [F3] gives $eV(A^+)=V(A)$ and $eU^+=U$, with the faithful supporting-block Morita equivalence and natural Hom comparison. Every simple constituent of $V(A^+)$ has the same entry-multiset central character as $A^+$; the bottom-row minimum argument forces every such label to be contractible. Hence the supporting central idempotent satisfies $fV(A^+)=V(A^+)$, and the Hom comparison identifies the original $\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U,V(A))$ with the entire large Hom module, rather than an arbitrary quotient of it. Step 4.1 therefore descends the same intrinsic Specht isomorphism to the original pyramid. [F3, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 Tilting images and full faithfulness. The opposite-parabolic flag coefficients are the actual tilting-character coefficients of [F1] and [F4]; exact $\pi$ carries each successive standard section to its Specht module by steps 4.1–5.1, so it preserves these flag multiplicities. For fullness, the local corner proof of [F2] applies: in the finite summand algebra $A$, $\pi$ is equivalent to $e(-)$ and has right adjoint $G(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{eAe}(eA,X)$. Its unit on a target with standard socle is injective and has off-standard cokernel. A tilting has standard socle from its standard flag and standard head from its costandard flag and simple-preserving restricted duality. Any map from it to the off-standard cokernel vanishes, since a nonzero quotient would have standard head. Adjunction therefore factors every map between its Schur images uniquely through the original target, proving full faithfulness on tiltings. [F1, F2, F4, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 Simple images and heads. The finite-W simple-image classification and the genuine Morita equivalence in [F2] and [F3] imply that $D(A)=\pi(L(A))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(V_c^{\otimes d},\mathsf L(A))$ is simple for $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, that these are distinct and exhaustive, and that $\pi(L(A))=0$ otherwise. For a standard label $A$, the cover $P(A)$ is an indecomposable summand of $T$, so $Y(A)=\pi(P(A))$ is an indecomposable projective. Its simple quotients are determined by $\operatorname{Hom}_{B_d}(Y(A),D(B))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(P(A),L(B))$, which has dimension $\delta_{A,B}$; this is the ordinary equivalence on $\operatorname{add}(T)$ and the simple-image computation. Thus $Y(A)$ has head $D(A)$. Lift the cover $P(A)\to L(A)$ through $N(A)\to L(A)$ using projectivity; the lift is surjective since the latter is the simple-head quotient and any proper submodule of $N(A)$ lies in its radical. Exactness yields $Y(A)\twoheadrightarrow S(A)\twoheadrightarrow D(A)$. Every nonzero quotient of the indecomposable projective $Y(A)$ has the same simple head $D(A)$: its kernel is contained in the unique maximal submodule. Therefore $S(A)$ has head $D(A)$. [F1, F2, F3, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Projective images. For $A\in\mathrm{Std}$, the preceding step shows that $Y(A)=\pi(P(A))$ is the indecomposable projective with simple head $D(A)$, hence its projective cover. Evaluation $T\otimes_{B_d}\pi(P(A))\to P(A)$ is an isomorphism because $P(A)\in\operatorname{add}(T)$: this is checked on $T$ and restricted to its idempotent summands. Thus $\pi^*\pi(P(A))\cong P(A)$. Off-standard projectives retain their actual images, and no projective-preservation assertion follows for them. [F2, step 6.2, algebra]

8.1 Multiplicities. Since $\pi$ is exact and its kernel is generated by the off-standard simples, the composition multiplicities of $S(A)=\pi(N(A))$ are the multiplicities of the simple $L(B)$ in $N(A)$ for $B\in\mathrm{Std}$; by the Fock-space dictionary [F4] the typed coefficient of the dual-canonical/canonical pairing equals $d_{B,A}(1)$, so $[S(A):D(B)]=[N(A):L(B)]=d_{B,A}(1)$; for $B\notin\mathrm{Std}$ the module $D(B)$ is zero and is not a simple Hecke label. All the identifications above are ungraded and taken at parameter $1$. [F2, F4, step 6.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- The intrinsic definition of $S(A)$ by parabolic induction replaces the faulty direct $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak p}$ identification of the source with the corner/regular-vector computation: the canonical colour fibre is only one of several fibres of $e_SV(A)$, and the corner operators supply the correct extension.
- The proof deliberately separates the stable-range corner computation (steps 1.1–5.1) from the exact-quotient consequences (steps 6.1–8.1); the latter only use exactness, the kernel description and the Fock dictionary, so they are insensitive to the choice of stable realization.

items.title: Category-O translation intertwines residue induction and restriction
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an admissible origin $c$; let
$f_i^{\mathcal O},e_i^{\mathcal O}$ be the residue translation functors on the
sum of parabolic blocks of
[[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]] and let
$f_i^{H},e_i^{H}$ be the Hecke residue functors of
[[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]].
Then there are natural isomorphisms
$$f_i^{H}\pi\cong\pi f_i^{\mathcal O},\qquad e_i^{H}\pi\cong\pi e_i^{\mathcal O},$$
where $\pi=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T,-)$ is the Schur functor of
[[def-the-higher-level-schur-weyl-projective-generator-and-schur-functor]],
compatible with the residue eigenvalue projectors, the units and counits of the
evaluation/coevaluation adjunction and its dual transported reverse adjunction, and with ordinary restricted duality and the $*$-duality of the
Hecke side. Consequently the ungraded Grothendieck operators at parameter $1$
agree and the Schur quotient induces a homomorphism for the enveloping-algebra Chevalley action. For
admissible nonintegral origins the category $\mathcal O$ side uses the genuine
typed coset realization, not an unqualified integer block. The statement
preserves the actual residue and standard filtrations; no graded parity or
Koszul lift is asserted by these ungraded suppliers.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The admissible origin $c$, the tensor objects $T_d=P_c\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ and $T_{d+1}=T_d\otimes V$, the Schur functors $\pi_d,\pi_{d+1}$, and the residue functors on both sides.

[F1] The O-side residue functors are exact, biadjoint, preserve projectives and injectives, commute with restricted duality, and agree with the generalized Casimir eigencomponents; their $K_0$ operators are the integrable Fock Chevalley action ([[def-residue-translation-functors-on-the-sum-of-parabolic-o-blocks]], [[lem-residue-casimir-operators-give-local-affine-hecke-actions]], [[thm-residue-translation-functors-give-the-integrable-fock-space-action]]).

[F2] The Hecke-side residue functors are exact, biadjoint, commute with the $*$-duality, and their operators are adjoint for the Cartan pairing ([[def-hecke-induction-and-restriction-functors-on-degenerate-cyclotomic-blocks]]).

[F3] The Schur functor is exact, kills exactly the off-standard simples and sends standards to intrinsic Specht modules. Its tensor detector $T_d$ is prinjective, its Hecke endomorphism algebra is $B_d$, and its Whittaker image $U_d$ is a projective generator of the corresponding finite-W image category. There are natural identifications $\gamma_M:\pi_dM\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{W_d}(U_d,\mathrm{Wh}M)$ and the coherent tensor isomorphisms $\nu_M:\mathrm{Wh}(M\otimes V)\cong\mathrm{Wh}(M)\circledast V$, with $\mu_d:U_d\circledast V\cong U_{d+1}$ intertwining the tower generators. In the stable realization $B_d$ is the full cyclotomic algebra, while content projections give the supported blocks. Every category-O projective has a copresentation $0\to P\to T_1\to T_2$ with $T_1,T_2\in\operatorname{add}(T_d)$. These are the actual Whittaker/Morita, copresentation and tensor contracts of [[thm-the-whittaker-functor-is-exact-and-fully-faithful-on-the-required-projectives]], [[def-the-whittaker-functor-from-the-relevant-parabolic-o-summand]], [[thm-higher-level-schur-weyl-endomorphism-isomorphism]] and [[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]].

[F4] The parabolic and genuine category-O interfaces with the typed coset realization for admissible nonintegral origins ([[def-integral-parabolic-category-o-block-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]).



## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The tensor identity $T_{d+1}=T_d\otimes V$, the actual Whittaker/Morita tensor data of [F3], and the two pairs of residue functors.

1.1 **Restriction uses the dual natural module.** For $N$ in the degree-$(d+1)$ summand and a basis $v_a$ of $V$ with dual basis $v^a$, tensor adjunction gives the natural map $\rho_N:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_{d+1},N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_d,N\otimes V^*)$, $\rho_N(h)(t)=\sum_a h(t\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$. Its inverse sends $g$ to $(t\otimes v)\mapsto(1\otimes\operatorname{ev}_v)g(t)$. These maps are basis-independent by coevaluation and evaluation and commute with the first $d$ tower generators, acting on the $T_d$ factors. Thus they identify restriction of $\pi_{d+1}N$ with $\pi_d(N\otimes V^*)$ after the appropriate degree/block projection. The natural and dual natural modules are distinct $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-modules; no identification between them is used. [F1, F3, construct, algebra]

1.2 **The induction map is an actual tensor map.** For $M$ of degree $d$, put $\tau_M:B_{d+1}\otimes_{B_d}\pi_dM\to\pi_{d+1}(M\otimes V)$, $b\otimes f\mapsto(f\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)\circ R_b$, where $R_b$ is the right action on $T_{d+1}$. The first $d$ generators act on $T_d$, so this expression is balanced over $B_d$ and is $B_{d+1}$-linear for the left-module convention; naturality follows by postcomposition. To prove it invertible, on the finite-W side form $\sigma_X(b\otimes g)=(g\circledast\mathrm{id}_V)\circ\mu_d^{-1}\circ R_b$. For $X=U_d$ this is the regular-module isomorphism $B_{d+1}\otimes_{B_d}B_d\cong B_{d+1}$. It remains an isomorphism on finite sums and summands. Every finite-W image object has a finite projective presentation by summands of finite sums of $U_d$, and both sides are right exact: induction is right exact, tensoring with $V$ is exact and Hom from $U_d,U_{d+1}$ is exact. Passing to cokernels proves $\sigma_X$ invertible for all $X$. The coherent $\gamma,\nu,\mu$ square of [F3] sends $1\otimes f$ by either route to $(\mathrm{Wh}(f)\circledast\mathrm{id}_V)\mu_d^{-1}$; $B_{d+1}$-linearity then makes the square commute on every $b\otimes f$. Consequently $\tau_M$ is invertible for every $M$. This presentation argument takes place in the finite-W image category, where $U_d$ is a full projective generator; it does not assert that $T_d$ is a full category-O generator. [F3, construct, algebra]

2.1 **The two residue projectors.** The tower's last dot on $T_d\otimes V$ is the tensor Casimir, with the normalization of [F1]. Hence $\tau$ intertwines its generalized-$i$ eigenprojector with the projector defining $f_i^{\mathcal O}$. On the dual tensor factor one has the actual operator identity $\Omega_{N,V^*}\rho_N(h)=-\rho_N(h\Omega_{T_d,V})-n\rho_N(h)$. Indeed $E_{ba}v^c=-\delta_{bc}v^a$ and equivariance of $h$ give the first term $-\sum_{a,b}h(E_{ab}t\otimes v_b)\otimes v^a$ and the second term $-n\sum_a h(t\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$, exactly that identity. Thus the last-dot generalized-$i$ projector corresponds to the dual-Casimir generalized-$(-n-i)$ projector, including its nilpotent part. This is the actual adjunction mate and agrees with the flag normalization in [F1]. Under $\rho$ the last-dot projector therefore corresponds to the generalized-$(-n-i)$ projector defining $e_i^{\mathcal O}$. Applying the source content projector $e_\alpha$ and target projector $e_{\alpha+\alpha_i}$ to steps 1.1–1.2 gives $u_{\alpha,i}\pi_{\alpha+\alpha_i}N\cong\pi_\alpha e_i^{\mathcal O}N$ and $B_{\alpha+\alpha_i}u_{\alpha,i}\otimes_{B_\alpha}\pi_\alpha M\cong\pi_{\alpha+\alpha_i}f_i^{\mathcal O}M$. Polynomial generalized-eigenspace projectors commute with these natural maps because the maps intertwine the operators, proving the asserted residue compatibility. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **The natural duality comparison.** The ordinary category-O duality $D$ uses matrix transpose and restricted weight-space duals. The product of the ground contravariant form and the natural-factor forms gives a nondegenerate detector form $(xtb,t')=(t,x^{\mathrm{tr}}t'b^*)$; the Casimir, crossings and content projectors are self-adjoint. Put $\delta M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,T_d)$ with $(bf)(m)=f(m)b^*$ and $X^\#=\operatorname{Hom}_{B_d}(X,B_d)$ with the same twist. The detector form gives an actual isomorphism $\beta:T_d\cong DT_d$, $\beta(t)(t')=(t,t')$. Exact restricted contravariant duality, with its canonical bidual map, consequently gives $\delta M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,T_d)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(M,DT_d)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g}(T_d,DM)=\pi_dDM$. Its explicit map is $f\mapsto[t\mapsto(m\mapsto(t,f(m)))]$; its inverse sends $g:T_d\to DM$ to $\beta^{-1}\circ Dg\circ\operatorname{bidual}_M:M\to T_d$. These maps are inverse by the symmetry and nondegeneracy of the form and the bidual identities, and the form's $*$-invariance makes them Hecke-linear. This is a canonical natural Hom-duality isomorphism; it requires neither dimensions of simple images nor self-duality of individual projective summands. Tensor-Hom gives $\delta\pi_d^*\cong\#$, while the symmetric trace of [F2] gives $\#\cong D_H$ by $h\mapsto\mathrm{tr}\circ h$. Define $\theta_M:M\to D\pi_d^*\delta M$ by $\theta_M(m)(t\otimes f)=(t,f(m))$. The displayed form identity makes it balanced over $B_d$ and $\mathfrak g$-linear. Applying $\pi_d$ gives a natural transformation $\pi_d\to\pi_dD\pi_d^*\delta\cong\#\pi_dD$ between exact functors. It is an isomorphism on $T_d$ and hence on its finite sums and summands. Apply the copresentations in [F3] to prove it an isomorphism on every projective, by exactness and kernels; then apply projective presentations to prove it on every object, by cokernels. Dualizing yields the natural comparison $\pi_dD\cong D_H\pi_d$. The product forms, tensor evaluation and trace form are the same forms used for the dual adjunctions; consequently this comparison identifies their dual unit/counit squares. Since the residue projectors are self-adjoint, it also commutes with each $f_i,e_i$ separately. Thus $Df_i\cong f_iD$ and $De_i\cong e_iD$. None of this identifies the usual tensor dual $V^*$ with $V$. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

3.2 **Grothendieck operators and quotient.** Exactness of $\pi$ and of the residue functors makes the natural isomorphisms of step 2.1 induce $[f_i^H][\pi]=[\pi][f_i^{\mathcal O}]$ and $[e_i^H][\pi]=[\pi][e_i^{\mathcal O}]$. On $G_0$, the source simple-class basis shows that $\ker[\pi]$ is exactly the span of the off-standard simple classes, and the induced map from this quotient onto $G_0(H)$ is an isomorphism. No isomorphism from the entire category-O Grothendieck group is asserted. On split projective groups only $\operatorname{add}(T)$ is equivalent to Hecke projectives; an ambient off-standard projective need not have projective image. These distinctions leave the displayed operator equalities intact. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Adjunction maps.** The first tensor unit is the coevaluation $m\mapsto\sum_a(m\otimes v_a)\otimes v^a$, and the tensor counit is evaluation. The induction/restriction unit is $z\mapsto1\otimes z$, and the counit is $b\otimes z\mapsto bz$. Substituting these formulas into $\tau$ and $\rho$ gives the same composite maps, term by term: coevaluation is precisely the sum in $\rho$, and evaluation cancels that sum by $v^a(v_b)=\delta_{ab}$. Restricting the commuting squares by the content and residue projectors proves compatibility for $f_i\dashv e_i$. For the reverse adjunction use the biadjoint mate maps supplied by [F1] and the symmetric-trace reverse adjunction of [F2]; transport the latter through $\tau,\rho$. The transported evaluation and coevaluation pair is the O-side biadjoint pair, since its dot and crossing mates agree with those in [F1], with the same trace normalization. Equivalently the reverse unit and counit are the dual mates of the first pair, so the same squares commute. The two pairs are thus compared with their transported normalizations; this is stronger than asserting abstract uniqueness of adjoints across a quotient. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 **Filtrations and boundaries.** Applying exact $\pi$ to the O-side residue standard flags preserves their successive quotients, and the intertwined generalized-eigenvalue projectors select the corresponding residue pieces. Admissible nonintegral origins retain the typed coset realization of [F4]; an integral highest-weight Fock interpretation is used only on its actual integral residue component. All comparisons here are ungraded at parameter one. Together with steps 2.1–3.2 this proves the statement. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, given] ∎

## Remarks

The raising tensor factor is $V$ and the lowering tensor factor is $V^*$. Their adjunction is evaluation/coevaluation. Restricted transpose duality fixes the natural factor and commutes with each residue functor; these are different constructions.

items.title: The degenerate affine Hecke relations on two tensor factors
items.statement: For gl_2, M=V and d=2, let P_ab permute factors a,b of V^tensor3. Then x_1=P_01, s_1=P_12 and x_2=P_02+P_12. Their eight-by-eight tensor-basis matrices satisfy s_1²=1, [x_1,x_2]=0, s_1 x_2−x_1 s_1=1 and x_2 s_1−s_1 x_1=1. For v_1 tensor v_2 tensor v_1, x_1 s_1 sends it to v_1 tensor v_1 tensor v_2, while s_1 x_2 sends it to the sum of that vector and the original. The commutator [s_1,x_2] is not literally1; the affine cross relation has the distinct x_1 on its other side.
items.strategy: Assume AC and work over C. Write each P_ab as its permutation of the eight binary words. Products of the three transpositions verify both affine relations. Expand [P_01,P_02+P_12]; the two oriented three-cycles cancel. Enumerate the basis words to check the displayed example and all matrix entries; this finite example tests the normalization, not the general proof.

items.title: A level-two cyclotomic polynomial from the highest-weight filtration
items.statement:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Take source-ordered row lengths $p=(1,2)$, so the column heights are
$q=(2,1)$, and let $N=3$, $n=2$, $c=(0,0)$. Number the boxes down the columns:
$1=(1,1)$, $2=(2,1)$, $3=(2,2)$. The pyramid nilpotent is $e=E_{23}$, and on
the one-step deformed tensor space $V_c^{\otimes1}=V=\mathbb C^3$ the operator
$x_1$ is
$$x_1=E_{23}+\operatorname{diag}(0,0,-1).$$
Its eigenvalue $0$ has multiplicity $2$ and eigenvalue $-1$ has multiplicity
$1$, with $-1$-eigenspace $\mathbb C(v_3-v_2)$; its minimal polynomial is
$x(x+1)$, with roots $a=(0,-1)$, and
$\Lambda=\Lambda_0+\Lambda_{-1}$. For every $d\ge1$ the raw tensor operator
$x_1$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ still has exactly this minimal polynomial, by the
column-filtration and leading-string argument. Consequently
$H_d(\Lambda)$ has dimension $2^dd!$, and at $d=1$ its image splits the two
stated eigenspaces.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The boxes $1=(1,1)$, $2=(2,1)$, $3=(2,2)$, the nilpotent $e=E_{23}$, and the roots $a_1=0+2-2=0$, $a_2=0+1-2=-1$.

1.1 The operators on $V$. For $d=1$ the cross-column correction in [F1] is absent and $\sum_j(c_{\mathrm{col}(j)}+q_{\mathrm{col}(j)}-n)e_{j,j}=\operatorname{diag}(0,0,-1)$, so $x_1=E_{23}+\operatorname{diag}(0,0,-1)$: explicitly $x_1v_1=0$, $x_1v_2=0$ and $x_1v_3=v_2-v_3$. Hence $x_1(x_1+1)=0$, the eigenspaces of $x_1$ are $\mathbb C v_1\oplus\mathbb C v_2$ for the eigenvalue $0$ and $\mathbb C(v_3-v_2)$ for the eigenvalue $-1$, and the minimal polynomial is exactly $x(x+1)$: $x_1\neq0$ since $x_1v_3=v_2-v_3\neq0$, and $x_1+1\neq0$ since $(x_1+1)v_1=v_1\neq0$. [F1, algebra]

2.1 All degrees and the cyclotomic quotient. By the minimal-polynomial clause of [F1], the operator $x_1$ on $V_c^{\otimes d}$ has minimal polynomial $\prod_j(x-a_j)=x(x+1)$ for every $d\ge1$, so the tensor action factors through $H_d(\mathbf a)$ with $\mathbf a=(0,-1)$, i.e. through $H_d(\Lambda)$ for $\Lambda=\Lambda_0+\Lambda_{-1}$; and by [F2] that quotient has dimension $2^dd!$. At $d=1$ the quotient is $\mathbb C[x]/(x(x+1))\cong\mathbb C\times\mathbb C$, acting on $V$ through $x_1$ as the two-dimensional algebra of operators that are scalar on each of the two eigenspaces of step 1.1; hence the image is semisimple and $V$ is the direct sum of those two eigenspaces. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: A Hecke action alone does not imply a double centralizer
items.statement:
**Refuted claim:** if a Hecke algebra action on $M\otimes V^{\otimes d}$ is
natural in the $\mathfrak g$-module $M$ and commutes with $\mathfrak g$, then
the two double centralizer equalities
$\varphi(U(\mathfrak g))=\operatorname{End}_{H_d}(M\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ and
$\psi(H_d)=\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}(M\otimes V^{\otimes d})$ hold.
items.strategy:
Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$ ([[def-classical-complex-matrix-lie-algebras]]), let $M=\mathbb C^2$ be the trivial $\mathfrak g$-module (all matrix units act by $0$), let $V=\mathbb C^2$ be the natural module ([[def-representation-of-a-lie-algebra]]), and let $d=1$. The Arakawa-Suzuki construction of [[def-arakawa-suzuki-casimir-operators-on-tensor-functors]] provides an action of $H_1=\mathbb C[x_1]$ ([[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]) on $M\otimes V\cong\mathbb C^4$ commuting with $\mathfrak{gl}_2$ ([[thm-the-casimir-and-place-permutation-operators-satisfy-degenerate-affine-hecke-relations]]).

**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The operators and modules of the Counterexample.

1.1 The Hecke action. By [F1] the generator $x_1$ acts as $0$ on $M\otimes V$, so the $H_1$-action is the evaluation action $x_1\mapsto0$ (the quotient $H_1/(x_1)=\mathbb C$ of [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] specialized to the scalar $0$). [F1, algebra]

2.1 The first centralizer. Since $H_1$ acts by the scalars $\mathbb C$ on the four-dimensional space, $\operatorname{End}_{H_1}(M\otimes V)=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb C^4)=M_4(\mathbb C)$, of dimension $16$. [step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The image of the enveloping algebra. By [F2] the image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ in $\operatorname{End}(M\otimes V)$ is the subalgebra $1\otimes M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension $4$. Hence the first double centralizer equality fails by a factor of $4$ in dimension. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The second centralizer. Writing an endomorphism as a $2\times2$ block matrix indexed by the basis of $M$, commutation with every $1\otimes E_{ij}$ forces each block to be a scalar matrix. Thus the $\mathfrak{gl}_2$-endomorphisms are $M_2(\mathbb C)\otimes1$, of dimension $4$, while $\psi(H_1)=\mathbb C\cdot\mathrm{id}$ has dimension $1$; hence the second equality also fails. The missing hypothesis is the truncated/deformed setup: the double centralizer theorem applies to the finite-W-algebra tensor space $V_c^{\otimes d}$ over a pyramid (equivalently, to $U(\mathfrak g^e)$ with the truncated polynomial algebra $\mathbb C_l[x_1,\dots,x_d]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]$), where the Hecke action is the cyclotomic quotient action and the algebra on the opposite side is the finite W-algebra, not $U(\mathfrak g)$ itself ([[thm-the-finite-w-and-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-actions-satisfy-double-centralizer]], [[def-the-type-a-finite-w-algebra-and-whittaker-category]]). [F2, step 3.1, given] ∎

items.title: Vust's double centralizer in a small stable range
items.statement:
Take the pyramid $\lambda=(1,1)$, so $n=2$, $l=1$, $q_1=2$, $N=2$, and $e=0$
(all boxes lie in one column, and the grading is concentrated in degree $0$):
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g^e=\mathfrak{gl}_2(\mathbb C)$, $\mathfrak m=0$,
$\mathbb C_1[x_1,\dots,x_d]=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_d]/(x_1,\dots,x_d)=\mathbb C$
and $\mathbb C_1[x]\rtimes\mathbb C[S_d]=\mathbb C[S_d]$. The stable range for
this $\lambda$ is $q_l\ge d$, i.e. $2\ge d$, so $d=1,2$ are exactly the positive stable
cases; degree zero is also stable. The example verifies Vust's double centralizer
([[thm-vust-double-centralizer-for-the-type-a-nilpotent-centralizer]]) in these
cases.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The data and conventions of the Example.

1.1 The case $d=1$. Here $B=\mathbb C[S_1]=\mathbb C$, so $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V)=\mathbb C\cdot1$ by Schur's lemma and the image $\varphi_1(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ by [F4]; both Vust identities reduce to these two equal-dimensional statements. [F4, F2, algebra]

1.2 The case $d=2$, second centralizer. By [F3], $V^{\otimes2}=S^2V\oplus\Lambda^2V$ with $\Lambda^2V$ one-dimensional and $S^2V$ three-dimensional irreducible. Since the flip acts by $+1$ on $S^2V$ and by $-1$ on $\Lambda^2V$, an endomorphism commuting with the $\mathbb C[S_2]$-action preserves each isotypic component, and its restrictions are arbitrary endomorphisms of the two (irreducible) components: $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C[S_2]}(V^{\otimes2})=\operatorname{End}(S^2V)\oplus\operatorname{End}(\Lambda^2V)$, of dimension $9+1=10$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 The case $d=2$, first centralizer. The image of $U(\mathfrak{gl}_2)$ in $\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes2})$ is the diagonal action on the two isotypic components, which by the mutual-centralizer statement of [F3] is the block-diagonal algebra $\operatorname{End}(S^2V)\oplus\operatorname{End}(\Lambda^2V)$, also of dimension $10$; hence $\varphi_2(U(\mathfrak{gl}_2))=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C[S_2]}(V^{\otimes2})$. The other direction, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes2})=\mathbb C[S_2]$, follows because $\psi_2$ is injective ($\dim\mathbb C[S_2]=2$ and the flip is not a scalar on $V^{\otimes2}$) and $\dim\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes2})=2$ by Schur's lemma applied to the two nonisomorphic components. [F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Range check. For $d\le2=q_l$ the stable-range hypothesis $q_l\ge d$ holds, and for $d=3$ it fails; this example therefore realizes the theorem exactly in its stable range and shows that the level-one case is the classical Schur-Weyl duality. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: A block idempotent corner outside the stable range
items.statement:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Take the pyramid $\lambda=(1,1)$, so $n=2$, $l=1$, $q_1=2$ and $N=2$, and let
$d=3$. The stable range $q_l\ge d$ fails, since $2<3$; the equivalent source
condition is that at least $3$ parts of $\lambda$ are equal to $l=1$, which is
false. With the origin $c=(0)$ one has $a_1=c_1+q_1-n=0$, so the level-one
cyclotomic quotient is $H_3(\Lambda)=\mathbb C[S_3]$, of dimension $6$, while
the image $H_3(\lambda,c)$ in
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}$, $V=\mathbb C^2$,
has dimension $5$. The example identifies the image as a block idempotent
corner $f\mathbb C[S_3]f$, verifying the central-corner statement of
[[def-stable-range-and-block-idempotent-for-higher-level-schur-weyl-duality]]
in the smallest non-stable case.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

**Given:** The image $\psi_3(\mathbb C[S_3])\subseteq\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes3})^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the Wedderburn blocks of [F3].

1.1 By [F2], the tensor space contains the trivial $S_3$ module with multiplicity four, the standard module with multiplicity two, and no sign module. The decomposition [F3] therefore makes the group-algebra image exactly $\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$, of dimension five. By classical Schur-Weyl duality [F2] this is $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{gl}_2}(V^{\otimes3})$, whereas $\dim\mathbb C[S_3]=6$. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 The killed sign block. By [F3] the block decomposition of $\mathbb C[S_3]$ is $\mathbb C\times\mathbb C\times M_2(\mathbb C)$; the one-dimensional sign block is spanned by the antisymmetrizer $a$ of [F4], which acts on $V^{\otimes3}$ by $0$. Hence the kernel of $\psi_3$ contains the sign block; since the image has dimension $5$ by step 1.1, the kernel has dimension $1$ and is exactly the sign block. So $\psi_3$ kills precisely the sign block and is injective on the direct sum of the trivial and standard blocks. [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The block idempotent corner. Let $f$ be the central idempotent of the trivial and standard blocks, so that $\mathbb C[S_3]f=\mathbb C[S_3]f^2$ is the corresponding two-sided ideal; its corner $f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ has dimension $1+4=5$ by [F3]. Multiplication by $f$, $x\mapsto fxf$, is an algebra surjection $\mathbb C[S_3]\twoheadrightarrow f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ whose kernel contains the sign block and has dimension $6-5=1$, hence is exactly the sign block; therefore $\mathbb C[S_3]/\!\ker\psi_3\cong f\mathbb C[S_3]f$ and the image $H_3(\lambda,c)=\psi_3(\mathbb C[S_3])$ is isomorphic to the block idempotent corner $f\mathbb C[S_3]f$, which is the central-corner form $fH_3(\mathbf a)f$ of the Definition. [F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The stable-range check. Here $q_l=q_1=2$ while $d=3$, so the stable range fails and the image is not the full algebra $H_3(\mathbf a)=\mathbb C[S_3]$ (which has dimension $6$); the corner of step 3.1 realizes the boundary case of the Definition, and the missing dimension $1$ is precisely the killed sign block. [F1, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎
